I can learn about things along the way, ask questions, and gradually improve my configurations.Automating almost everythingSomething I’ve also finally managed to do is automate most of the build, patch, and deployment processes for my infrastructure.A lot of the work involved in self-hosting isn’t particularly exciting. Keeping track of new releases, updating container image tags, building images, and deploying configuration changes are all things that need to be done regularly.I still remember what updating a service used to look like: bumping the version and adjusting the Docker Compose file on my laptop, pushing the changes to the Git remote, SSHing into the server, pulling the changes, and finally deploying them. Now, a single Git push is enough. If a push is even necessary.With Renovate, I no longer need to actively keep track of most software updates. It creates pull requests for me, and often, all I need to do is review and merge them. I can even do that on my phone while sitting on the sofa.Pushing changes or merging a pull request triggers the corresponding GitHub Actions or Forgejo Actions workflows, which take care of building and deploying everything.Of course, there’s nothing particularly groundbreaking about any of this. DevOps has been around for a long time, and none of these automation tools require AI. But AI has helped me put all these pieces together in a way that I previously never quite got around to doing.And the nice thing about automating these tasks is that the benefits extend well beyond the initial setup. I now have less tedious work to do every time I want to change something or update a service.Back to more powerful hardwareAs I’ve started hosting more things again, I’ve also moved more of my services from my VPS to my home server.For a while, I was using an HP t640 thin client as my home server. However, with more things I wanted to run, I decided to switch back to my ASRock DeskMini A300, which had been sitting unused for some time. I’m thinking about repurposing the t640 as a “router on a stick”, though.I even took the opportunity to upgrade its CPU from an AMD Ryzen 5 2400G to a Ryzen 5 PRO 4650G and replaced the stock AMD cooler with a quieter Noctua cooler. Noise was the main reason I switched to the t640 in the first place.It’s nice to put some hardware I already owned back to use rather than buying an entirely new machine. I also managed to get both the CPU and the cooler for a good price through a classifieds site.Having some additional computing power available gives me more room to experiment. And there’s something quite satisfying about having a small box at home running a growing collection of services that I use in my everyday life.Building my own toolsBut it’s not just about self-hosting existing software. AI has also changed how I approach problems for which there isn’t an existing piece of software that does exactly what I want.Previously, I would often spend quite some time searching for a suitable open-source project, comparing different alternatives, and figuring out how to make one of them work for my particular use case.These days, for smaller problems, building my own solution has become a much more attractive option.I’ve recently built tools to automatically download invoices, e-papers or Linux ISOs.I can build (or have AI build) these tools in Go, my preferred programming language, and tailor them to my exact needs.They don’t need to support every possible use case, have an elaborate user interface, or be particularly interesting to anyone other than me. I don’t need to turn every little tool into a proper open-source project with extensive documentation and support for other people’s use cases. They just need to solve my problem.What I particularly enjoy is how well this complements my increasingly automated infrastructure. Building a small tool has become easier, and so has building a container image for it, deploying it, and keeping it running.The entire process, from having an idea to having something actually running on my home server, requires much less effort than it used to.Just because I can doesn’t mean I shouldOf course, there are downsides to all of this.Every additional service is another thing that needs to be maintained. AI-generated software isn’t exempt from bugs, security issues, or technical debt. And having an AI agent make changes to my infrastructure doesn’t absolve me of the responsibility of understanding those changes.There’s also the temptation to build or deploy things simply because I can. When implementing an idea becomes so easy, it’s perhaps more important than ever to occasionally ask myself whether it’s actually worth implementing in the first place.On the other hand, self-hosting is a hobby for me. Not everything I do needs to be economically sensible or particularly useful. Sometimes, experimenting with something new is the whole point.And with much of the routine maintenance automated, adding another service doesn’t necessarily mean adding as much recurring work as it used to.A somewhat ironic development?I find it somewhat ironic that AI, a technology largely dominated by substantial tech companies, is helping me become a little less dependent on those very companies in other areas of my digital life.I’m aware that this also creates a new kind of dependency. But the software and infrastructure configurations I create with the help of AI can continue to exist independently of the AI services I used to create them. And since I mostly use open-weight models, I have a wide range of providers to choose from.What I appreciate most, however, isn’t necessarily the time I’m saving. It’s that I’m more inclined to actually pursue the little ideas I have.I’m trying out technologies I’ve been curious about for years. I’m automating things that I’ve wanted to automate for a long time. I’m building little tools for myself. I’m tinkering with hardware again.AI hasn’t fundamentally changed why I like self-hosting. I still enjoy having control over my digital life, learning new things, and tinkering with technology.It’s just removed a lot of the friction that made me lose some of my enthusiasm for it over the years.And now, I’m having a lot of fun with it again.

In a recent development, in the past, I would sometimes put off certain changes simply because I didn’t feel like spending an evening reading changelogs and documentation or troubleshooting issues. It’s not that I couldn’t have done these things before. I’ve always liked the idea of declaratively configuring an entire system; I even used it on my laptop during my Linux honeymoon phase. But it’s also something I probably wouldn’t have invested enough time in to get working on my own before. Even with the help of AI, it still took me half a day when I set it up a few months ago. Without AI, it would probably have taken me at least a week.AI makes experimenting with unfamiliar technologies much more approachable. I don’t necessarily need to understand every little detail before I can get started. I can learn about things along the way, ask questions, and gradually improve my configurations.Automating almost everythingSomething I’ve also finally managed to do is automate most of the build, update, and deployment processes for my infrastructure.A lot of the work involved in self-hosting isn’t particularly exciting. Keeping track of latest releases, updating container image tags, building images, and deploying configuration changes are all things that need to be done regularly.I still remember what updating a service used to look like: bumping the version and adjusting the Docker Compose file on my laptop, pushing the changes to the Git remote, SSHing into the server, pulling the changes, and finally deploying them. Now, a single Git push is enough. If a push is even necessary.With Renovate, I no longer need to actively keep track of most software updates. It creates pull requests for me, and often, all I need to do is review and merge them. I can even do that on my phone while sitting on the sofa.Pushing changes or merging a pull request triggers the corresponding GitHub Actions or Forgejo Actions workflows, which take care of building and deploying everything.Of course, there’s nothing particularly groundbreaking about any of this. DevOps has been around for a long time, and none of these automation tools require AI. But AI has helped me put all these pieces together in a way that I previously never quite got around to doing.And the nice thing about automating these tasks is that the benefits extend well beyond the initial setup. I now have less tedious work to do every time I want to change something or update a service.Back to more powerful hardwareAs I’ve started hosting more things again, I’ve also moved more of my services from my VPS to my home server.For a while, I was using an HP t640 thin client as my home server. However, with more things I wanted to run, I decided to switch back to my ASRock DeskMini A300, which had been sitting unused for some time. I’m thinking about repurposing the t640 as a “router on a stick”, though.I even took the opportunity to upgrade its CPU from an AMD Ryzen 5 2400G to a Ryzen 5 PRO 4650G and replaced the stock AMD cooler with a quieter Noctua cooler. Noise was the main reason I switched to the t640 in the first place.It’s nice to put some hardware I already owned back to use rather than buying an entirely new machine. I also managed to get both the CPU and the cooler for a good price through a classifieds site.Having some additional computing power available gives me more room to experiment. And there’s something quite satisfying about having a small box at home running a growing collection of services that I use in my everyday life.Building my own toolsBut it’s not just about self-hosting existing software. AI has also changed how I approach problems for which there isn’t an existing piece of software that does exactly what I want.Previously, I would often spend quite some time searching for a suitable open-source project, comparing different alternatives, and figuring out how to make one of them work for my particular use case.These days, for smaller problems, building my own solution has become a much more attractive option.I’ve recently built tools to automatically download invoices, e-papers or Linux ISOs.I can build (or have AI build) these tools in Go, my preferred programming language, and tailor them to my exact needs.They don’t need to support every possible use case, have an elaborate user interface, or be particularly interesting to anyone other than me. I don’t need to turn every little tool into a proper open-source project with extensive documentation and support for other people’s use cases. They just need to solve my problem.What I particularly enjoy is how well this complements my increasingly automated infrastructure. Building a small tool has become easier, and so has building a container image for it, deploying it, and keeping it running.The entire process, from having an idea to having something actually running on my home server, requires much less effort than it used to.Just because I can doesn’t mean I shouldOf course, there are downsides to all of this.Every additional service is another thing that needs to be maintained. AI-generated software isn’t exempt from bugs, security complications, or technical debt. And having an AI agent make changes to my infrastructure doesn’t absolve me of the responsibility of understanding those changes.There’s also the temptation to build or deploy things simply because I can. When implementing an idea becomes so easy, it’s perhaps more vital than ever to occasionally ask myself whether it’s actually worth implementing in the first place.On the other hand, self-hosting is a hobby for me. Not everything I do needs to be economically sensible or particularly useful. Sometimes, experimenting with something new is the whole point.And with much of the routine maintenance automated, adding another service doesn’t necessarily mean adding as much recurring work as it used to.A somewhat ironic development?I find it somewhat ironic that AI, a technology largely dominated by big tech companies, is helping me become a little less dependent on those very companies in other areas of my digital life.I’m aware that this also creates a new kind of dependency. But the software and infrastructure configurations I create with the help of AI can continue to exist independently of the AI services I used to create them. And since I mostly use open-weight models, I have a wide range of providers to choose from.What I appreciate most, however, isn’t necessarily the time I’m saving. It’s that I’m more inclined to actually pursue the little ideas I have.I’m trying out technologies I’ve been curious about for years. I’m automating things that I’ve wanted to automate for a long time. I’m building little tools for myself. I’m tinkering with hardware again.AI hasn’t fundamentally changed why I like self-hosting. I still enjoy having control over my digital life, learning new things, and tinkering with technology.It’s just removed a lot of the friction that made me lose some of my enthusiasm for it over the years.And now, I’m having a lot of fun with it again.

Not everything I do needs to be economically sensible or particularly useful. Sometimes, experimenting with something new is the whole point.And with much of the routine maintenance automated, adding another service doesn’t necessarily mean adding as much recurring work as it used to.A somewhat ironic development?I find it somewhat ironic that AI, a technology largely dominated by big tech companies, is helping me become a little less dependent on those very companies in other areas of my digital life.I’m aware that this also creates a new kind of dependency. But the software and infrastructure configurations I create with the help of AI can continue to exist independently of the AI services I used to create them. And since I mostly use open-weight models, I have a wide range of providers to choose from.What I appreciate most, however, isn’t necessarily the time I’m saving. It’s that I’m more inclined to actually pursue the little ideas I have.I’m trying out technologies I’ve been curious about for years. I’m automating things that I’ve wanted to automate for a long time. I’m building little tools for myself. I’m tinkering with hardware again.AI hasn’t fundamentally changed why I like self-hosting. I still enjoy having control over my digital life, learning new things, and tinkering with technology.It’s just removed a lot of the friction that made me lose some of my enthusiasm for it over the years.And now, I’m having a lot of fun with it again.

With Renovate, I no longer need to actively keep track of most software updates. It creates pull requests for me, and often, all I need to do is review and merge them. I can even do that on my phone while sitting on the sofa.Pushing changes or merging a pull request triggers the corresponding GitHub Actions or Forgejo Actions workflows, which take care of building and deploying everything.Of course, there’s nothing particularly groundbreaking about any of this. DevOps has been around for a long time, and none of these automation tools require AI. But AI has helped me put all these pieces together in a way that I previously never quite got around to doing.And the nice thing about automating these tasks is that the benefits extend well beyond the initial setup. I now have less tedious work to do every time I want to change something or update a service.Back to more powerful hardwareAs I’ve started hosting more things again, I’ve also moved more of my services from my VPS to my home server.For a while, I was using an HP t640 thin client as my home server. However, with more things I wanted to run, I decided to switch back to my ASRock DeskMini A300, which had been sitting unused for some time. I’m thinking about repurposing the t640 as a “router on a stick”, though.I even took the opportunity to upgrade its CPU from an AMD Ryzen 5 2400G to a Ryzen 5 PRO 4650G and replaced the stock AMD cooler with a quieter Noctua cooler. Noise was the main reason I switched to the t640 in the first place.It’s nice to put some hardware I already owned back to use rather than buying an entirely upcoming machine. I also managed to get both the CPU and the cooler for a good price through a classifieds site.Having some additional computing power available gives me more room to experiment. And there’s something quite satisfying about having a small box at home running a growing collection of services that I use in my everyday life.Building my own toolsBut it’s not just about self-hosting existing software. AI has also changed how I approach problems for which there isn’t an existing piece of software that does exactly what I want.Previously, I would often spend quite some time searching for a suitable open-source project, comparing different alternatives, and figuring out how to make one of them work for my particular use case.These days, for smaller problems, building my own solution has become a much more attractive option.I’ve recently built tools to automatically download invoices, e-papers or Linux ISOs.I can build (or have AI build) these tools in Go, my preferred programming language, and tailor them to my exact needs.They don’t need to support every possible use case, have an elaborate user interface, or be particularly interesting to anyone other than me. I don’t need to turn every little tool into a proper open-source project with extensive documentation and support for other people’s use cases. They just need to solve my problem.What I particularly enjoy is how well this complements my increasingly automated infrastructure. Building a small tool has become easier, and so has building a container image for it, deploying it, and keeping it running.The entire process, from having an idea to having something actually running on my home server, requires much less effort than it used to.Just because I can doesn’t mean I shouldOf course, there are downsides to all of this.Every additional service is another thing that needs to be maintained. AI-generated software isn’t exempt from bugs, security issues, or technical debt. And having an AI agent make changes to my infrastructure doesn’t absolve me of the responsibility of understanding those changes.There’s also the temptation to build or deploy things simply because I can. AI has also changed how I approach problems for which there isn’t an existing piece of software that does exactly what I want.Previously, I would often spend quite some time searching for a suitable open-source project, comparing different alternatives, and figuring out how to make one of them work for my particular use case.These days, for smaller problems, building my own solution has become a much more attractive option.I’ve recently built tools to automatically download invoices, e-papers or Linux ISOs.I can build (or have AI build) these tools in Go, my preferred programming language, and tailor them to my exact needs.They don’t need to support every possible use case, have an elaborate user interface, or be particularly interesting to anyone other than me. I don’t need to turn every little tool into a proper open-source project with extensive documentation and support for other people’s use cases. They just need to solve my problem.What I particularly enjoy is how well this complements my increasingly automated infrastructure. Building a small tool has become easier, and so has building a container image for it, deploying it, and keeping it running.The entire process, from having an idea to having something actually running on my home server, requires much less effort than it used to.Just because I can doesn’t mean I shouldOf course, there are downsides to all of this.Every additional service is another thing that needs to be maintained. AI-generated software isn’t exempt from bugs, security issues, or technical debt. And having an AI agent make changes to my infrastructure doesn’t absolve me of the responsibility of understanding those changes.There’s also the temptation to build or deploy things simply because I can. When implementing an idea becomes so easy, it’s perhaps more important than ever to occasionally ask myself whether it’s actually worth implementing in the first place.On the other hand, self-hosting is a hobby for me. Not everything I do needs to be economically sensible or particularly useful. Sometimes, experimenting with something new is the whole point.And with much of the routine maintenance automated, adding another service doesn’t necessarily mean adding as much recurring work as it used to.A somewhat ironic development?I find it somewhat ironic that AI, a technology largely dominated by massive tech companies, is helping me become a little less dependent on those very companies in other areas of my digital life.I’m aware that this also creates a new kind of dependency. But the software and infrastructure configurations I create with the help of AI can continue to exist independently of the AI services I used to create them. And since I mostly use open-weight models, I have a wide range of providers to choose from.What I appreciate most, however, isn’t necessarily the time I’m saving. It’s that I’m more inclined to actually pursue the little ideas I have.I’m trying out technologies I’ve been curious about for years. I’m automating things that I’ve wanted to automate for a long time. I’m building little tools for myself. I’m tinkering with hardware again.AI hasn’t fundamentally changed why I like self-hosting. I still enjoy having control over my digital life, learning new things, and tinkering with technology.It’s just removed a lot of the friction that made me lose some of my enthusiasm for it over the years.And now, I’m having a lot of fun with it again.

AirPods Pro 3 one year later: Still the best, and getting even better

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been just over a year since Apple released AirPods Pro 3, and I can confidently say I’ve worn them every day since.
  • According to recent reports, while the changes to AirPods Pro 3 fit have been controversial to some consumers, I’ve been thoroughly impressed over the last year.
  • Industry observers note that one feature I haven’t found myself using (or noticing) very often is the heart rate sensor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been just over a year since Apple released AirPods Pro 3, and I can confidently say I’ve worn them every day since. After a year of heavy use, I’m even more convinced that AirPods Pro 3 are the best money you can spend on Apple gear (especially at current sale pricing).

According to recent reports, while the changes to AirPods Pro 3 fit have been controversial to some consumers, I’ve been thoroughly impressed over the last year. I find them incredibly comfortable, and I absolutely notice the improvement in noise cancellation enabled by the updated in-ear fit. The sound quality, of course, is also excellent, and is made better by the updated shape.

Industry observers note that one feature I haven’t found myself using (or noticing) very often is the heart rate sensor. This is probably because I always wear an Apple Watch. Apple states that AirPods Pro 3 and Apple Watch can work together to get you the most accurate heart rate data possible. I assume this happens in the background, but I never notice or think about it.

An interesting twist to AirPods Pro 3 is that they actually have worse battery life on paper than AirPods Pro 2.

Recent findings suggest that I haven’t noticed the overall lower battery life at all. On long travel days, however, I absolutely appreciate the longer battery life from the buds themselves. I can now comfortably wear them from my departure airport to my arrival airport on most travel days. And I don’t have any challenges just placing my AirPods Pro 3 on a Qi charger on my desk to refuel.

One thing I love about AirPods is that they continuously get better with software updates. AirPods Pro 3 are no different. In addition to bug fixes and performance improvements, here are some of the latest features that have come to AirPods Pro 2 since they were released:.

Here’s what I wrote in my AirPods Pro 3 review last year:.

I often tell people that AirPods are the best bang-for-your-buck product in Apple’s lineup. They’re one of my most-used Apple products, and I’m sure I could do some math to prove they have the lowest cost-per-use of anything I own. AirPods Pro 3 are the best $249 you can spend with Apple today, and they feel like a turning point in what we should expect from the category going forward.

Industry observers note that one year later, I stand by this paragraph. Also, note that I wrote $249 in that paragraph. Right now, AirPods Pro 3 are on sale for $149. That is an absolutely absurd value. If you’re on the fence, there’s never been a better time to join the AirPods Pro 3 club.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it's finally Thanksgiving weekend, and it's time to sit back, relax, eat, and be merry. And watch some good ol' classics on the boob tube. Like every other major streaming service, Hulu dropped a mountain of new movies into its library at the start of the month. That's hundreds of fresh options staring back at you tonight ... and, let's be honest, most of them aren't worth your time.

According to recent reports, so I've done the digging for you, combing through everything new on Hulu this November to spotlight the three films that are actually worth your evening. Curious what made the cut before you commit your downtime? That's certainly to be expected. Here's the lowdown on three new Hulu movies that have earned a spot on your watchlist.

OK, yes, Halloween has come and gone, but bear with us. This 2023 Warner Bros. animated comedy is a fun pick for family movie night nevertheless. Deep beneath ancient Egypt, three mummies live in a hidden underground city: a runaway princess, a former royal charioteer and his brother. A chain of mishaps lands them in present-day London, and soon they're chasing a ring swiped by a greedy archaeologist named Lord Carnaby.

It has been revealed that the English voice cast is loaded with British talent, including Sean Bean as the Pharaoh, Eleanor Tomlinson as Princess Nefer and Hugh Bonneville as villain Carnaby. It's colorful, fast and silly enough to keep younger kids happy, with a baby crocodile sidekick thrown in for good measure. It's a fun thing to keep the kids entertained with, at the very least.

Angelina Jolie returns to Paris for this drama from French director Alice Winocour, playing Maxine Walker, an American filmmaker who arrives for Fashion Week and is blindsided by a life-changing medical diagnosis. The film weaves together three women whose paths cross amid the glamour and not-so-pretty face of haute couture, with Jolie's Maxine alongside a rising model (Anyier Anei) and a makeup artist (Ella Rumpf. Jolie has called it her "most personal" role, using the loss of her own mother to cancer to fuel her performance.

According to recent reports, alan Ritchson, TV's "Reacher," headlines this action-comedy as Hank Malone, a former soldier yanked into a frantic race against the clock when a medical delivery makes him the target of a ruthless cartel, with an innocent child's life depending on whether he can get the cargo where it needs to go. Owen Wilson plays his partner, with Rodrigo Santoro as a member of the cartel and Leila George co-starring. It plays a bit like an extended "Reacher" episode, but Ritchson and Wilson make for easy firm if you're in the mood for a straightforward action ride. And who isn't after inhaling their Thanksgiving dinner?

#155346. Latest Update: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

📅 13 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 24m • 📚 Deep Dive (4872 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.
  • It has been revealed that emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the massive positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo.
  • Sources indicate that signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

It has been revealed that emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the massive positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Sources indicate that signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the latest year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Recent findings suggest that emery stated: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

Recent findings suggest that “Of course there is still work to do but they indicated they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another vital player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

It has been revealed that england centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

According to recent reports, while some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

According to recent reports, the Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

Industry observers note that it was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Industry observers note that before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

Sources indicate that villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

According to recent reports, it became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK.

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

In a recent development, luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s.

Recent findings suggest that 💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7.

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the latest Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34.

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo.

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

There will be five added minutes.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

According to recent reports, the Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Industry observers note that aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a massive summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

Industry observers note that “I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

Sources indicate that PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

Does Bill Ackman Know Something Wall Street Doesn't? The Billionaire Investor Keeps Buying a Tech Stock That's Now Down 44% Over the Past Year.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Ackman has also purchased stakes in several hyperscalers driving the artificial intelligence revolution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Bram Berkowitz – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:20AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Netflix ›.

Recent findings suggest that bill Ackman and his team at Pershing Square, the parent organization of the investment manager Pershing Square Capital Management, run a concentrated portfolio. Ackman is not afraid to play contrarian, and he isn't afraid to hold stocks long term, which is a different strategy from that employed by most standard hedge funds.

Ackman has also purchased stakes in several hyperscalers driving the artificial intelligence revolution. Given Pershing's impressive track record and Ackman's huge following, investors are always curious about what the billionaire is buying.

In the third quarter, Ackman and his team continued to load up on one tech stock that's down by about 44% over the past year. Does he know something Wall Street doesn't?

Recent findings suggest that bill Ackman. Image source: Getty Images.

Nearly all sectors have been disrupted by the emergence of artificial intelligence, even companies that were considered cutting-edge tech stocks very recently. The video streaming business faces threats too. Investors are now concerned about lower barriers to entry for content creation, as well as the rising popularity of short-form content from platforms like YouTube.

It has been revealed that these concerns have spooked investors about the outlook for streaming giant Netflix (NFLX +2.13%). The stock, which hit an all-time high in June 2025, has been crushed over the past year.

Reports of declining viewer engagement have led many to believe an industrywide shift is underway, and Netflix's management team more or less acknowledged those concerns on its Q3 earnings call last month.

Sources indicate that "Turning to the U.S., the other region, our engagement is solid, and it will allow us to continue to grow as we have for the last several years," co-CEO Greg Peters noted on the call. "We know that we can do better, and that better is our upside.".

Recent findings suggest that while Ackman and Pershing had previously owned a stake in Netflix several years ago, they closed it. Then, they opened a new position in the second quarter of 2026. In Q3, Pershing increased that position by 18%; as of the end of the quarter, Netflix made up 3.5% of the portfolio.

In its June interim report, Pershing said that it believes investors are underestimating the cost of creating long-form, high-quality content, which it said remains "among the most compute-intensive tasks." Pershing also noted that the popularity of short-form content has had no significant effect on Netflix's results.

NASDAQ · As of 10:38 AM ET 11/27/26.

It has been revealed that in Pershing's Q3 update earlier this month, the company reiterated its belief in Netflix and noted investors are focusing too much on engagement as measured by viewer watch time. It believes the company's foray into live programming and other upcoming content will make this less of a concern.

Pershing is also excited about Netflix's advertising business.

In a recent development, "Advertising revenue continues to scale rapidly, and the lower-priced ad-supported tier is meaningfully expanding Netflix's addressable market," Pershing wrote. "AI should further enhance the business by improving content recommendation and ad targeting algorithms, driving efficiencies and enabling fresh forms of interactive and personalized content.".

Pershing believes Netflix can generate double-digit percentage revenue growth over the next few years, while compounding earnings at 20% annually.

There's no question that the rise of short-form content poses a challenge for companies like Netflix, which, once upon a time, may not have considered short form as a competitor.

In a recent development, I agree with Ackman and his team that the market may be underestimating how difficult it is to replicate high-quality, long-form content with cheaper latest technologies. I still think that is evident whether you look at successful Netflix shows or at long-form podcasts that continue to do well. Netflix has also raised subscription prices across all its tiers and continues to see healthy retention, according to management.

Recent findings suggest that netflix will likely need to invest in new types of content and keep adjusting its strategy to stay ahead in the entertainment space, but the tech giant has the expertise and resources to do so. AI can also help advance and optimize its existing business.

While nobody knows exactly how AI and short-form content will continue to affect the streaming video space, I like the risk-reward proposition here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A one-line prompt that makes ChatGPT leak its private opinion of you, in a pretty funny format: a WhatsApp group chat where the AI models gossip about their users.
  • Also worth trying on Claude, Gemini, or any assistant that's been accumulating your chat history.
  • Instead of a summary, the model commits to the bit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A one-line prompt that makes ChatGPT leak its private opinion of you, in a pretty funny format: a WhatsApp group chat where the AI models gossip about their users.

Also worth trying on Claude, Gemini, or any assistant that's been accumulating your chat history.

Instead of a summary, the model commits to the bit. It invents a group chat, something like "Customers We Can't Figure Out", puts the other AI models in it, and lets them gossip. About you. Using everything it has quietly learned from your conversations.

It has been revealed that one person's actual output, shared with permission. Translated from Turkish; his name and a few identifying details have been swapped for generic ones. Everything else is exactly as the model wrote it.

Shared by its author, translated from Turkish, with his name and identifying details generalized. The "recursion, no base case" line is doing a lot of work here.

According to recent reports, run the prompt, read your leaked group chat, and notice two things: how hard you laugh, and how much of it is true. Both measurements are the point.

Sources indicate that I'm not affiliated with OpenAI and this may indeed be a viral marketing idea they're testing. But I had such a laugh, I figured others would have some fun with it as well and decided to share it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Enterprise software and cloud infrastructure company Oracle (ORCL) recently announced better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

Industry observers note that after hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he said.

"We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," said DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

While Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as new contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

DiFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

"RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," said Gesuale.

The 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space company with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

Gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst said, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

In a recent development, gesuale ranks No. 369 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17%. See Rocket Lab Statistics on TipRanks.

Industry observers note that J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth recently upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to buy from hold and raised his price target to $820 from $640. Despite the year-to-date underperformance of META, the 5-star analyst still sees significant upside, as Meta is in the early stages of launching frontier models and AI-powered offerings beyond advertising, particularly the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.

"Frontier models are at the core of Meta's product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence," remarked Anmuth.

In the summer of 2025, Meta set a goal to rebuild its Meta Superintelligence Labs team and deliver frontier AI models within a year, the analyst stated. The team appears to have met its goal, rapidly advancing from the rollout of Muse Spark 1.1 in July to Muse Spark 1.3, which is competitive with Claude and GPT models, Anmuth said.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Meta's Watermelon product will expand opportunities in consumer products, business intelligence, and Family of Apps engagement, the analyst stated. The product will enhance internal operations and overall efficiency, said Anmuth, who's confident of Meta's ability to bring consumer-driven AI products to its extensive user base of 4 billion and views its distribution network as a competitive advantage.

While Meta has focused on frontier models and AI product development, Anmuth also sees solid opportunity in its AI infrastructure capacity, which he believes will support future compute needs.

Industry observers note that anmuth ranks No. 832 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of about 9.40%. See Meta Platforms Financials on TipRanks.

Anthropic’s Lock-Up Expirations Start Dec. 15. Here’s What Investors Should Know Before Then.

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (813 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that anthropic (ANT +8.52%) raised a record amount of capital with its initial public offering (IPO).
  • The offering’s underwriters exercised their greenshoe option, buying an extra 147 million shares for just over $12 billion.
  • In a recent development, but Anthropic's public offering accounted for only about 6% of its fully diluted share count, which includes stock options, restricted stock units, and convertible notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adam Levy – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:24AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

Industry observers note that anthropic (ANT +8.52%) raised a record amount of capital with its initial public offering (IPO). It sold 980 million shares to the public at $83 each, raising about $81 billion.

The offering’s underwriters exercised their greenshoe option, buying an extra 147 million shares for just over $12 billion. The AI lab also raised $26 billion in concurrent private placement deals with several big tech companies alongside its IPO. All in all, that brought the tech giant $119.5 billion before underwriting expenses.

In a recent development, but Anthropic's public offering accounted for only about 6% of its fully diluted share count, which includes stock options, restricted stock units, and convertible notes. The rest of the shares — those held by insiders and pre-IPO stakeholders — remain locked up. But the expiration of the first phase of that lock-up comes in just a few weeks on Dec. 15.

There are some vital details investors should know before the first lock-up expiration.

It has been revealed that anthropic's valuation at its IPO was about $1.5 trillion. Given that massive market cap, staggering its lock-up expiration helps prevent a flood of shares from weighing down the stock price. Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +3.55%) is taking a similar approach with its IPO lock-up.

Anthropic outlined its lock-up expiration calendar in its prospectus. Of note, Anthropic has two share classes: Class A shares are ordinary shares of capital stock; Class N shares are those that were issued to strategic investors, such as tech companies investing in its private placement offerings. Class N shares convert to Class A shares upon sale to unaffiliated parties.

Industry observers note that A huge number of shares are set to be added to the stock’s float — the pool of tradable shares — over the next year. The current float is set to double with the first four lock-up expirations between December and February, and it'll increase by another 70% from there after Anthropic's first earnings report as a publicly traded manufacturer.

Recent findings suggest that those early lock-up expirations will be a major test of just how much appetite there is for Anthropic shares. SpaceX faced similar dynamics. While the first expiration went well, with the market fully absorbing the latest shares without much impact on the price, its more recent lock-up expirations haven't gone as smoothly for shareholders.

According to recent reports, another vital detail about Anthropic's share lockup that you might notice is that Class N share lockups are backloaded. That's because shareholders with more than a 0.5% ownership stake are subject to the full 365-day lockup period, while smaller shareholders will be able to sell all of their stock after 180 days.

In a recent development, the 0.5%-plus ownership group includes names like Alphabet and Amazon. They'll likely seek to reduce their market influence on the stock price until they can sell all their shares.

Sources indicate that the substantial fear for investors is that a flood of newly tradable shares will increase selling pressure on the stock, sending the price lower as Anthropic’s early investors and employees look to cash out. Indeed, that's the whole reason why Anthropic scheduled a much more spaced-out lock-up schedule than the typical IPO.

While the increase in float could push the stock price down, investors know these selling events are coming. That could lead them to discount shares ahead of key lock-up expiration dates, making it easier for the market to absorb sellers.

That's exactly what we saw with SpaceX. Shares actually climbed 6% on the date of its first lock-up expiration.

NASDAQ · As of 10:41 AM ET 11/27/26.

Over time, Anthropic's share price moves should more closely reflect changes in the business's value. Short-term selling pressure from lock-up expirations could provide discounts that long-term investors can take advantage of to build their positions.

But investors shouldn't take an unlock-related sell-off in Anthropic shares as a good reason to buy the stock. There are considerable risks for the AI stock that need to be factored into even the rosiest outlooks for the firm. If you don't buy it with a wide enough margin of safety, you could face some significant losses if your forecast proves too optimistic. Determining the price you're willing to pay for the stock before a potential selling event can help you capitalize on the potential opportunity it creates.

Applying for Social Security and Medicare at the Same Time in 2027? 3 Things You Need to Know.

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (427 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:28AM EST.
  • Industry observers note that if you're turning 65 in 2027, you'll soon be signing up for Medicare, and of course, you'll have the option to claim Social Security, too, assuming you're not already receiving checks.
  • Here are three things you should be aware of before you apply for Social Security and Medicare in 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:28AM EST.

Industry observers note that if you're turning 65 in 2027, you'll soon be signing up for Medicare, and of course, you'll have the option to claim Social Security, too, assuming you're not already receiving checks. But these are major financial decisions, so it's worth thinking them through carefully before you decide.

Here are three things you should be aware of before you apply for Social Security and Medicare in 2027.

You are within your rights to claim Social Security at age 65, but doing so is technically considered early claiming and carries an early withdrawal penalty. To avoid this, you must delay your Social Security application until your full retirement age (FRA). This is 67 if you were born in 1960 or later. Older adults have slightly younger FRAs.

According to recent reports, this doesn't mean you shouldn't claim Social Security at 65. It can still be the right move for you if you aren't able to work, have little personal savings, or have a short life expectancy.

But if you don't need your checks right now, you might get a larger lifetime benefit by waiting a few more years before you apply. If you'd like, you can continue delaying Social Security until you qualify for your largest benefit at age 70.

Industry observers note that when you're on both Medicare and Social Security benefits, the government withholds your Medicare Part B premiums from your Social Security checks. This gives you one less bill to worry about each month.

In 2027, the Part B premium will be $209.40 for most seniors, though wealthy Americans will pay more. If you opt to claim Social Security later, you will have to pay these premiums out of your own pocket until you apply for Social Security.

There's no rule saying that you must apply for Social Security and Medicare at the same time. Choose your Social Security claiming age based on your estimated life expectancy, finances, and personal preferences. Consider a variety of claiming ages before you settle on one to make sure you're comfortable with the trade-offs of your decision.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Where it goes from here is unknown, but the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio, also known as the Shiller P/E ratio, is still elevated at about 38.
  • It is unsettling in the near term, but in the long-term view, it creates a buying opportunity for investors, as Warren Buffett summed up in Berkshire Hathaway's (BRKA -0.04%) (BRKB +0.12%) 2008 letter to shareholders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:30AM EST.

The major indexes entered the Thanksgiving holiday in correction territory, with the S&P 500 down about 10% since its all-time closing high on Oct. 6 and the Nasdaq Composite off 17% since then.

Where it goes from here is unknown, but the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio, also known as the Shiller P/E ratio, is still elevated at about 38. Although that's down from more than 40 in October, it is still as high as it's been since the dot-com boom.

It is unsettling in the near term, but in the long-term view, it creates a buying opportunity for investors, as Warren Buffett summed up in Berkshire Hathaway's (BRKA -0.04%) (BRKB +0.12%) 2008 letter to shareholders.

In a recent development, the 2008 shareholder letter came out on Feb. 27, 2009, in the teeth of the financial crisis. The S&P 500 had plummeted 37% in 2008, and as of the day the investor letter was released, it had dropped another 19% year to date to 735.

The S&P 500 was not done falling at that point; it sank another 8% to bottom out at 676 on March 9.

According to recent reports, these were clearly difficult times, certainly the worst since the 2000-2002 dot-com bust and worse than anything since. But Buffett was energized by the opportunity before him.

According to recent reports, buffett was busy that quarter, adding shares of Wells Fargo (WFC +1.53%), U.S. Bancorp (USB +1.53%), Johnson & Johnson (JNJ +0.25%), and Union Pacific (UNP +0.04%), among others.

It proved to be a smart move, as one year after the letter was posted, Feb. 26, 2010, the S&P 500 closed at 1,104, up 50% in a year. As for Berkshire Hathaway's performance, its B shares jumped 56% from $51.28 on Feb. 27, 2009, to $80.13 on Feb. 26, 2010.

Recent findings suggest that the lesson for investors is to, like Buffett, take a long-term view and seize the opportunity to add good-quality merchandise, or in this case, stocks, to your portfolio. Given the fact that the S&P 500 has averaged about a 10% annual total return over its history, markets have always recovered from downturns and moved higher.

It's not always easy to determine which discounted stocks are likely to recover and which aren't. The best strategy is to look for stocks with valuation metrics, like the P/E ratio, that are below historical averages. Then check their earnings, outlook, industry, and market share to make sure their decline is not a function of longer-term problems. If you are unsure, invest in an exchange-traded fund that tracks the S&P 500 or Nasdaq.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, as of this writing (after the market close on Nov.
  • For four years, the stock market has appeared invincible, unfazed by tariffs or wars.
  • Industry observers note that for starters, there's no way to predict the future based on the past.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Steven Porrello – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:45AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

According to recent reports, as of this writing (after the market close on Nov. 25), the S&P 500 index (^GSPC +1.13%) has declined in nine of the past 10 trading sessions. Yet despite the sell-off, the benchmark index remains up about 5% for the year; ditto for the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +0.92%) and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +1.63%) indexes, which are also up in spite of recent pullbacks.

This continues a trend. For four years, the stock market has appeared invincible, unfazed by tariffs or wars. That resilience, however, may have reached its breaking point. And if the scales are is falling from investors' eyes, the result might spell bad news for a certain group of stocks.

Industry observers note that for starters, there's no way to predict the future based on the past. This is even more the case when we're observing a pattern that has occurred only a handful of times in history.

Nevertheless, much wisdom can come from studying and observing past markets, which can give us some clues about the risks of historically high valuations.

One way to gauge the stock market's valuation is the Shiller price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, also known as the CAPE ratio.

According to recent reports, like the traditional P/E ratio, the Shiller is a quick way to evaluate whether stocks are cheap or expensive. Unlike the traditional P/E, however, which relies on a single year of earnings, the Shiller uses average inflation-adjusted earnings during the past 10 years. This helps smooth out the effects of economic cycles (like recessions and bull markets); it's not perfect, but it can come in handy when comparing an index's valuation over time.

It has been revealed that since January 1871, the Shiller P/E has averaged roughly 17.5. As of Nov. 25, it stood at about 37.9, or more than double its historical average. Suffice it to say, stocks are historically expensive.

Only six times in history has the Shiller P/E clocked in above 30, with most of those occurring after 1999. The previous five were followed by painful stock market declines. And if recent history can tell us anything about today's premium valuations, it's that growth stocks could take the biggest hit.

Industry observers note that just months before the bubble popped in 2000, the Shiller P/E reached an all-time high of roughly 44. What followed was one of Wall Street's most painful bear markets, during which the Nasdaq plunged 80% from its peak in March 2000 to its trough in October 2002.

It has been revealed that although the dot-com damage was widespread, the losses were not evenly distributed. Indeed, growth stocks bore the brunt. Between 2000 and 2002, the Russell 1000 Growth Index (IWF +1.43%) plunged 57%, compared with a decline of 26.5% for the Russell 1000 Value Index (IWD +1.02%).

IWD Total Return Level data by YCharts.

It has been revealed that A similar disparity emerged during the bear market of 2022. As the Federal Reserve aggressively hiked interest rates to combat surging inflation, the Russell 1000 Growth Index tumbled about 32%. Its value counterpart, meanwhile, declined 19%.

In a recent development, does this mean investors should abandon growth stocks right now? Not quite. Although growth stocks are historically vulnerable to sharp pullbacks, bear markets also present some of the best opportunities to buy them.

According to recent reports, for example, shares of the iShares Russell 1000 Growth ETF (exchange-traded fund) purchased at the trough of the dot-com bear market would have delivered a roughly 1,600% return if held through today. Its value counterpart also delivered strong returns, albeit considerably smaller (about 998%).

Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events?
  • There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.
  • Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It has been revealed that it was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes highlighted he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

Recent findings suggest that the one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

It has been revealed that you would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Sources indicate that top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

Recent findings suggest that trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Industry observers note that leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6.

Sources indicate that it was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

Industry observers note that it’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in Fresh Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have latest signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.
