💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stock markets remain volatile as investors weigh uncertainty in the Middle East, rising interest rates and concerns about the artificial intelligence (AI) trade.
  • Recent findings suggest that given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking a stable income stream can enhance their portfolios with the addition of dividend stocks.
  • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stock markets remain volatile as investors weigh uncertainty in the Middle East, rising interest rates and concerns about the artificial intelligence (AI) trade.

Recent findings suggest that given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking a stable income stream can enhance their portfolios with the addition of dividend stocks. In this regard, tracking recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks that are backed by strong financials.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Industry observers note that integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is the first dividend pick. Earlier this month, the company paid a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share. At an annualized dividend of $7.12 per share, CVX offers a dividend yield of about 3.5%.

Industry observers note that after a meeting with senior leadership, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on CVX and raised his price target to $240 from $225. Among the key takeaways Mehta emphasized was that Chevron is building a solid pipeline of promising international exploration projects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa and the Eastern Mediterranean. In particular, he mentioned the focus on Venezuela, where Chevron expects to more than double gross production to 600 kbd from about 280 kbd by 2031, using three joint ventures.

Mehta also noted Chevron's efforts to deploy new technologies, especially in shale and tight-oil operations. CVX is focused on boosting productivity and efficiency to maximize free cash flow, he added.

In a recent development, initiatives such as artificial lift optimization, AI and machine learning, and advanced chemical treatments are expected to improve recovery by about 10% in latest wells. Consequently, capital spending per barrel in U.S. shale is projected to fall 25% in 2026, with total Permian spending dropping below $3.5 billion.

Mehta also mentioned that Chevron sees power as a growth opportunity and is using its U.S. natural gas portfolio, key equipment and partnerships to meet rising demand. Notably, Chevron recently signed a 20-year power purchase deal with Microsoft (MSFT) to supply 2.67 GW of behind-the-meter capacity. This project, called Kilby, is expected to see its first power delivery in 2028 and generate mid-teens returns and long-term cash flows.

It has been revealed that mehta ranks No. 536 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 11.3%. See Chevron Statistics on TipRanks.

Enterprise Products Partners (EPD) is a master limited partnership (MLP) that provides midstream energy services to producers and consumers of natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), crude oil, refined products and petrochemicals. With a quarterly cash distribution of 56 cents per common unit ($2.24 per common unit annualized), EPD offers a yield of about 6%.

Industry observers note that following a recent call with the tech giant, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on EPD with a price target of $42. The analyst slightly lowered her estimates for the second half of 2026, citing margin and volume normalization, though demand dynamics remain strong.

While the 5-star analyst expects a sequential decline due to normal seasonality and normalization following high spreads in the first half of the year, she still expects EPD to report another solid quarter (Q3 2026) and enter 2027 with a favorable setup. Ahead of Q3 earnings, Scotto expects investors to focus on export demand durability, EPD's ability to profit from spot cargo sales and growth in Permian volumes.

Scotto continues to expect $150 million of common unit buybacks per quarter in the second half of 2026. She expects buybacks to increase to $200 million per quarter in 2027, as capex spending declines and free cash flow improves.

Sources indicate that in total, Scotto is bullish on EPD and views it as a core MLP holding that has both offensive and defensive characteristics. The analyst praised EPD's diverse asset base as ensuring stable cash flows. Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026, plus more AI workplace updates

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption.
  • During the keynote for the organization’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella confirmed Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.
  • Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the organization’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella confirmed Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several newly introduced Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft noted. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

Microsoft also revealed Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s latest Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Microsoft said the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

Industry observers note that “Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft mentioned.

The tech giant added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

Nadella also confirmed a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. At the moment in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up promptly,” Microsoft stated of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

Microsoft also declared that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can swiftly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft declared a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Sources indicate that agent 365, which Microsoft confirmed last year, is the firm’s observability platform. Microsoft remarked Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft demonstrated how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a fresh way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise intends.

  • According to recent reports, it seems like all year in 2026, investors have been worrying and debating about the idea of an artificial intelligence (AI) bubble in the stock market.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Gran – Nov 27, 2026 at 5:46AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.

According to recent reports, it seems like all year in 2026, investors have been worrying and debating about the idea of an artificial intelligence (AI) bubble in the stock market. Well, wonder no more: the bubble seems to be bursting. In the past month, the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 index has declined by 16%. Between Oct. 6 and Nov. 20, the index nearly reached "bear market" status, with a decline of 19.84%.

The S&P 500 index (^GSPC +1.13%)is not immune to this sell-off. That benchmark index has lost nearly 11% in the past month.

Big stock market sell-offs like the one we're going through right now aren't fun or easy. It's natural to feel worried or afraid for the future. But in a strange way, I'm in a pretty good mood this week. That's because, over my years of investing through bear markets and economic crises, I've learned a new mindset for stock market sell-offs.

I want to share my one-sentence mindset shift that helps me stay calm and confident during stock market crashes. Maybe it will work for you, too.

This mindset sounds simple, but I have repeated it to myself many times over the years when the stock market is tanking: "You don't need the money today.".

It has been revealed that here's what I mean by this. I am a long-term investor. The money that I've put into the stock market is not money that I need today. It's not my emergency fund. It's not my vacation fund. It's not money that I need to pay bills this month or the next. It's long-term money. "Leave it alone for 20 years" money.

Because of this long-term perspective, I can (most of the time) stay calm when the stock market is crashing. I'm not trying to get rich quick by flipping stocks for a fast profit. I'm trying to buy and hold a diversified portfolio of stocks, including low-cost index funds, that will let me build wealth gradually over the next few decades.

According to recent reports, I don't need the stock market to make me rich today. I hope that the stock market will make me richer over the next 20 years.

According to recent reports, but just saying "I'm a long-term investor" isn't enough to build wealth. The stock market must deliver significant gains. Fortunately, that tends to happen. As part of that long-term perspective, I'm a student of stock market history.

The S&P 500 index has delivered 9.98% annualized returns since 1928. Think of all the stressful times, economic crises, and global catastrophes that have happened during those 98 years. That 9.98% average annual return happened despite the Great Depression. It includes World War II, and the 1970s stagflation, and the 2000 dot-com bust, and the 2008 global financial crisis.

Recent findings suggest that even with all the booms and busts along the way, the S&P 500 has been a strong investment for long-term shareholders. In the past 16 years since it was released in Sept. 2010, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO +1.17%) has delivered average annual returns of about 14.8%. VOO has delivered about 12% annualized returns in the past five years (as of Oct. 31).

NYSEMKT · As of 10:40 AM ET 11/27/26.

Even if the next few years have lower stock market returns, buying S&P 500 ETFs tends to be a great move -- if "you don't need the money today.".

  • Recent findings suggest that after reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one.
  • For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over.

Recent findings suggest that after reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one. Who knows, you might end up caving in and treating yourself to a brand-new device? (You’ve been warned.).

For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

It has been revealed that the iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays.

The compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

The Duo is a great gift for someone who’s said they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV demonstrates on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use.

Recent findings suggest that the iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity.

The Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos.

It has been revealed that multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them.

It has been revealed that perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.

For the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.).

The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

Industry observers note that it’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

Like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job.

The Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

According to recent reports, some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr.

Industry observers note that the phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

Recent findings suggest that for most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography.

The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference.

In a recent development, the Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr.

No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

Microsoft’s fresh Licensed Weights lets businesses customize AI models with their own data

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (513 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella unveiled several latest models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company.
  • Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.
  • MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella unveiled several latest models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Manufacturer to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, stated during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft said it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman said during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

According to recent reports, western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman stated of the latest coding model the tech giant announced at Ignite.

The tech giant also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

According to recent reports, ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

In a recent development, but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

Recent findings suggest that this is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some vital ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful.

With the repository added, you can install it with:.

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

Recent findings suggest that it’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

Uber, Nuro and Lucid Begin Fully Driverless Testing With Their Luxury Robotaxi

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies stated Tuesday.
  • The partnership, confirmed in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles.
  • Recent findings suggest that now, the partnership is ready to take its next big step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies stated Tuesday.

The partnership, confirmed in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles. Autonomous rides take place aboard the Lucid Gravity robotaxi, which I had the opportunity to see first at a CES showcase in January (in the form of a “production intent design”), and then on the road this summer, with a safety driver behind the wheel.

Recent findings suggest that now, the partnership is ready to take its next big step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies said. They strategy to launch commercial robotaxi operations in the first quarter of 2027 in the San Francisco Bay Area, before expanding to Houston later next year. Lucid will begin manufacturing the first vehicles designed specifically for the commercial launch fleet “in the coming weeks.” Uber looks to deploy around 35,000 Lucid vehicles equipped with the Nuro Driver in the coming years in “dozens” of cities.

“Removing the safety operator from behind the wheel is an crucial milestone in our partnership with Nuro and Lucid, and a testament to all three partners’ focus on executing against our shared roadmap,” Samarth Kejriwal, Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility, said in a statement. “As we prepare for our first driverless passenger rides in the coming months, we’ll be working closely together to refine our operations, infrastructure and the in-cabin experience to ensure a safer, more comfortable ride.”.

Nuro says it’s been conducting “round-the-clock autonomous testing of the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area and Houston” since December 2025, with a safety driver in the vehicle who can take over if needed.

Recent findings suggest that in May, Nuro received a California Public Utilities Commission Drivered Pilot Permit, giving the company the green light to conduct pilot testing for an autonomous passenger service with a safety driver. Nuro also received a California Department of Motor Vehicles Driverless Testing Permit in April, allowing it to test self-driving vehicles without a safety driver.

Uber’s partnership with Nuro and Lucid is just one of dozens it has with other AV companies, including Waymo, Zoox, Avride, Wayve and May Mobility. Adding driverless options to an app that’s likely already on someone’s phone could increase their chances of giving the experience a try — despite the trepidation many people have about self-driving vehicles.

Recent findings suggest that the Lucid Gravity robotaxi can seat up to six passengers, unlike rides from Waymo and Zoox that seat up to four. It has plenty of legroom and ample space for luggage in the back. The vehicle’s sensor suite is equipped with cameras, lidar sensors and radars for autonomous navigation.

In a recent development, it’s been a big year for autonomous vehicles, and it appears 2027 will be no different. The rapid expansion of AVs comes amid heightened scrutiny. Last week, the California DMV banned Waymo’s robotaxis from state freeways after a series of high-profile incidents — after which Waymo paused all of its freeway rides. Waymo, the largest player in the AV space, has been involved in a number of other safety incidents as it expands to more cities. Over the years, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has launched investigations into other AV companies, including Zoox and Tesla.

It’s against this landscape — and the full-speed-ahead race toward autonomy — that Nuro, Uber and Lucid will soon publicly debut their own robotaxi.

In a recent development, some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving update. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

The v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch customers can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

According to recent reports, also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s latest model worth it?

It has been revealed that constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

In a recent development, wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how quickly it can drain.

Also: Galaxy Watch 9 review: Health data overload, but built for the future.

The patch improves battery life without customers having to take any action or change any settings — the Google Play Services version 26.45 works quietly under the hood.

That’s not the only Google Play Services revision that Wear OS smartwatch users can take advantage of. Another recent update lets users view on their phone a larger preview of any watch face they want to install on their smartwatch.

  • Brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a new brand via AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

Salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a new brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

Retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

Shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

Recent findings suggest that 1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

The survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

Agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent users using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

In a recent development, retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

In a recent development, today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

#155308. CNET Survey: $75 Billion in Packages Could Be at Risk of Holiday Porch Theft

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1573 w)
📖 Baca

CNET Survey: $75 Billion in Packages Could Be at Risk of Holiday Porch Theft

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Big holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a strategy to protect your package from porch pirates.
  • Recent findings suggest that CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts.
  • But leaving your packages up for grabs could be a big risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Big holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a strategy to protect your package from porch pirates.

Recent findings suggest that CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts. This year, the average package value is $276.24, and 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or caught an attempted theft within the past year. Yet 20% of US adults don’t use security devices due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees.

But leaving your packages up for grabs could be a big risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered. On the other hand, some bad actors don’t seem to mind being caught in the act on home security cameras, so are they really enough to deter bad actors? And what more can you do to protect your deliveries?

CNET’s findings show that some US adults have dealt with porch theft firsthand: 8% had packages meant for themselves or their households stolen within the past year, and 5% had a delivered gift stolen. Very few (1%) caught a theft in the act on a video doorbell or security camera.

Meanwhile, many US adults know someone who fell victim to package theft — 13% know a neighbor or community member who had a package stolen within the past year, and 12% know someone who doesn’t live in their community who has.

“Close to a third of our respondents are personally acquainted with package theft, which is still a high number compared to other challenges like break-ins,” said CNET’s senior home security editor, Tyler Lacoma. “Thieves generally look for crimes of opportunity, and few things are easier than a package left on a doorstep, especially if nobody is home.”.

Surprisingly, most US adults (72%) haven’t experienced package theft or know anyone who has.

Even though the percentages above may seem low, Lacoma stated that package theft typically increases during the holidays when thieves know more deliveries are likely, and new porch theft tactics are always on the horizon.

There are reports of thieves trying Wi-Fi jamming to disable live security camera footage while they steal packages. And findings show that some are installing spy cams in high-value neighborhoods to learn your home’s layout and habits to take your packages shortly after they’re delivered. In recent years, pirates have even tracked shipping labels for high-value tech, like iPhones, to steal the package within minutes of arrival.

So while the majority of US adults haven’t fallen victim, that shouldn’t be a sign to shrug off the concern or relax your home security measures. Instead, now’s the time to initiative how to safely store your packages if they’re delivered while you’re away.

Online shopping and deliveries to your door can be a convenient way to check off holiday wish lists, but the average package value this holiday season is less than last year. CNET found that US adults plan to have an average of $276.24 in holiday packages delivered during this holiday season. That’s $23.82 less than last year’s average of $300.06.

By generation, Millennials also have a lower estimated average package value than last year, with an average of $227.25, compared to their 2025 package value of $307.47 — an $80.22 difference, while Gen Z’s package value is only about $7 less than last year. But any package’s value is still worth taking precautions to help prevent it from being stolen.

In a recent development, lacoma has thoughts on why that might be. In short, lower spending could mean fewer packages.

Recent findings suggest that “I wonder if people have also simply gotten fewer packages in general this year due to tariffs, inflation and tech prices. That could pull these numbers down,” remarked Lacoma. But there’s a high chance that could be the case considering CNET’s 2026 annual holiday survey, which found that US adult tech spending is down to $808 — which is $123 less than last year’s average of $931.

Thieves may not always know what’s in boxes they’re stealing but they’re willing to take a chance. We asked US adults which items were stolen in package thefts in the past year to give you a sense of what’s at risk.

Among the items stolen, apparel and accessories were the most common goods stolen (40%). That’s followed by toys and games (23%). Then there are everyday home basics, like decor, cookware and small appliances (19%).

But personal tech devices and accessories are still among the items stolen. Small accessories like phone chargers and cases are most common (16%) among tech-related packages stolen. They are followed by audio gadgets like headphones and Bluetooth speakers, along with streaming devices and soundbars (11%, respectively).

Still, more costly tech like gaming consoles (10%), computers and laptops (9%) and smart home devices (6%) are among devices stolen.

In a recent development, you shouldn’t leave your packages up to chance. That’s why Lacoma recommends a few safer options to ensure your packages are stored securely after they’re delivered, even beyond keeping an eye on your doorbell or security camera. Instead, keep your packages out of sight with tactics like a delivery box with a code or key or ask for an in-garage delivery.

Industry observers note that “Delivery boxes have reached a latest level of popularity in recent years as an effective way to stop porch pirates completely. However, Amazon’s Key service that delivers to your garage is an alternative,” said Lacoma. “Either way, you’ll need to trust delivery people to handle your shipments, unless you want to arrange for pickup at a nearby shipping center, which some people like to combine with other holiday errands.”.

If you don’t want to install a newly introduced security feature, try scheduling your packages to arrive when you know you’re home, requiring a signature from someone you trust or changing your delivery location to a pickup spot, like UPS’ Hold for Pick-Up locations or Amazon Lockers.

Home surveillance, like outdoor security cameras and video doorbells, can deter package thieves who don’t want to risk getting caught on camera. But US adults have mixed feelings about their effectiveness in protecting against package theft.

There are two deterrents that are keeping US adults from having security devices — cost and privacy. Findings show that 20% of US adults lack home security measures due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees. That’s followed by 9% who don’t want to use cameras because of privacy concerns.

It has been revealed that “Fortunately, the right home security picks can solve both these problems,” said Lacoma. “Brands like Tapo, Eufy, Aqara and even Google Nest offer package detection and alerts for free, so you don’t have to worry about extra fees.”.

It has been revealed that if you’re looking for a camera that’s off-the-grid, consider the Arlo Go 2. It’s an LTE camera, so it uses a cellular data connection instead of Wi-Fi. It still finds a signal, supports app operation and live video viewing. If you’re looking for a power-over-Ethernet camera that uses a cable connection, the Reolink Duo 3 is a good choice.

Recent findings suggest that lacoma added that many companies also offer ways to use local video storage and local AI detection so nothing is stored in the cloud. There are also features, such as customizable privacy zones, to minimize privacy concerns when used with the right precautions.

In a recent development, among all US adults, only 14% have security devices with a monthly subscription that lets them save or playback video. By comparison, 12% have security devices but no subscription.

Those percentages could be low for a few reasons, including the overall perception of how helpful surveillance and security really are against porch theft. Eleven percent of US adults don’t think security devices deter porch thefts. It’s a valid concern since 4% fell victim to package theft or an attempted theft despite having security devices. And some US adults (9%) use security devices to get proof of a theft after the fact — not to prevent it.

According to recent reports, but that doesn’t mean you should ignore the possibility of package theft — especially during the holidays. Even if you don’t want to install cameras or newly introduced security devices, make a plan to protect your packages and avoid the headache of package theft over the holidays.

“Remember, the simple presence of a security camera is enough to make many thieves look elsewhere – interviews have confirmed it,” noted Lacoma. “And with today’s phone alerts about package detection, you can usually check on a package only seconds after it appears, or bring up footage if it unexpectedly vanishes, letting you take action fast. Upcoming practices like delivery boxes or in-garage delivery help address risks in concrete ways, too.”.

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,016 adults. Fieldwork was undertaken between Oct. 23–27, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus).

The $75 billion figure was calculated by multiplying the average value of deliveries each US adult expects to receive by the 2025 US population of adults ages 18 and over calculated by the US Census Bureau.

  • According to recent reports, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

According to recent reports, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Significant Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

According to recent reports, if Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The tech giant already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

In a recent development, gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro plan, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent owners may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

Recent findings suggest that as with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

Industry observers note that the feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US users can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

It has been revealed that the change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The new landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

“Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

Sources indicate that also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Industry observers note that “You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release said. Google’s fresh Memory summary feature for Gemini lets users view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

Neocloud manufacturer CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

According to recent reports, after a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. Devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

Sources indicate that overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Tuesday, Bambu Lab took the wraps off its third-generation 3D printer, the P3C. It brings to the mainstream the company’s “tool changer” technology, which was previously reserved for higher-end, flagship models like the $2,500 H3C. Given the P3C costs less than half the bigger model, it might be the perfect gift to get your favorite 3D printing hobbyist for Black Friday.

The major deal here is the introduction of the Swaptek 7-tool changer, which allows you to switch to a different color or material in just 6 seconds, preventing you from having to stop and clean the nozzle every time. The technology produces significantly less waste and allows you to create faster prints.

The tool changer technology also allows you to mix different materials with less of a fuss, so you can use a typical rigid plastic and something like a flexible rubber in a single pass without stopping. It can switch between different nozzle sizes in one job. You can switch between  0.2 mm, 0.4 mm, 0.6 mm and 0.8 mm midprint.

Industry observers note that the P3C ships with an integrated sealed AMS 3P filament management system that can store up to seven spools, each of which is on an independent feed path to the printer. You can also connect up to four external AMS units, supporting up to 22 colors.

In a recent development, the P3C is more than just a 3D printer. The Swaptek system supports interchangeable craft tools, letting you cut, draw or emboss on materials.

In a recent development, bambu Lab also included a few features that make the P3C more approachable to newcomers. The P3C provides full-auto calibration, automatically aligning nozzle offsets and multi-tool heads so you don’t have to do it yourself. There’s also a built-in AI monitoring system that can detect complications like nozzle clogs and purge-bin jams early on. A new health management system will no longer spit out vague or obscure errors when something goes wrong. Instead, the new system will explain the matter in plain language and provide step-by-step troubleshooting right on the screen.

Sources indicate that CNET’s 3D printing expert, James Bricknell, hasn’t been able to test Bambu Labs’ latest model yet but is excited about it. “While the P3C didn’t arrive in time for a hands-on, it’s built with the same design language and hardware support as the recently released H3C. If it is anywhere near as good, and I think that’s likely, it’ll be at the top of any serious 3D printing enthusiast’s wish list.”.

The P3C 3D printer AMS combo is available now worldwide for $1,149. The combo includes the printer, AMS 3P as well as 5 0.4mm standard PrintTools. Two slots are left open for you to customize. This combo option comes with virtually everything you need to get started printing your works of art and more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is kicking off a new and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful new features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

Industry observers note that first up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone consumers in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the latest Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

According to recent reports, the upcoming Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Industry observers note that along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

#155300. A Human and an AI Model (Apparently) Solved the Riemann Hypothesis: What it Means for Future of Math

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2175 w)

A Human and an AI Model (Apparently) Solved the Riemann Hypothesis: What it Means for Future of Math

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2175 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the Riemann Hypothesis is one of math’s oldest and most famous unsolved problems.
  • Alpöge made the announcement on Friday in a four-page document (PDF) on his personal web page.
  • It has been revealed that “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge said in the announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Riemann Hypothesis is one of math’s oldest and most famous unsolved problems. It was originally put forward as a problem in 1859 by Bernhard Riemann, and professional and amateur mathematicians alike have made thousands of attempts to solve it. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge has apparently solved the problem with the help of AI, showing that in the battle of humans versus AI, the real winner might be both of them working together.

Alpöge made the announcement on Friday in a four-page document (PDF) on his personal web page.

It has been revealed that “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge said in the announcement. “In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too.”.

The actual hypothesis itself isn’t the biggest deal since all it does is make it easier to see the distribution of prime numbers. However, math didn’t come to a screeching halt just because the hypothesis hadn’t been proven. There are hundreds of other math theorems along with algorithms and cryptographic encryption methods that operate based on the assumption that the Riemann Hypothesis is true.

According to recent reports, the Riemann Hypothesis is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute’s seven Millennium Problems for this very reason. If Alpöge really did solve the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude’s help, it would remove a metaphorical logjam that’s been gumming up the works for over a century and a half. Most of those hundreds of math theorems would be proven as true overnight, and all of those algorithms and encryption methods would be validated. That would make solving the Riemann Hypothesis one of the greatest mathematical breakthroughs in history.

Industry observers note that “It is certainly an exciting time,” Paul Milewski, head of the department of mathematics at Penn State, remarked in an email to CNET. “The Riemann Hypothesis (or any big theorem) is often not the ‘goal’ of mathematics. They are set up as grand challenges that require the development of fresh tools, new results along the way and new understanding. It is the ‘voyage’ and not the destination that matters the most.”.

Industry observers note that as such, the mathematics community wasted no time testing the proof to see whether it was true. Two groups — Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative — independently verified the proof, with many other researchers running their own tests and coming to the same conclusion.

“We have full confidence that Alpöge’s proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him on the achievement,” the two groups said in a joint statement on Saturday.

According to recent reports, this is certainly an exciting discovery, but it’s not without its obstacles. Alpöge’s proof was a staggering 250,000 pages of some of the most complex math ever written by a human or a machine. Alpöge provided 17 million lines of Lean code, a programming language specifically made for writing and checking proofs, and that’s how researchers were able to check the work and show it to be true.

In a recent development, the problem is that the average novel is about 300 pages, and that means that Alpöge’s AI-assisted proof is approximately 833 novels’ worth of complex math. For reference, the longest work ever produced is World-2023, which holds the Guinness World Record at 100,100 pages. That book is 19 feet tall, and Alpöge’s proof is two and a half times longer.

Industry observers note that despite the logic being verified as true through Lean code, Alpöge still has a major problem. So far, none of the mathematicians or researchers who have attempted to read it have been able to understand what it says.

“I do not understand, and I suspect no human completely understands,” Jon Keating, professor of mathematical physics at the University of Oxford, stated in a Numberphile YouTube video. “When I look at that, I’m completely in awe and in wonderment.”.

According to recent reports, for the problem to be fully solved, the proof has to be read, analyzed and simplified so that it can be translated into readable mathematics, which Alpöge claims in his announcement that he’s in the process of doing. All of this has to be done so that Alpöge can publish it in a peer-reviewed journal in such a way that his peers can actually read it. It is only after the mathematics community scrutinizes and accepts Alpöge’s proof that it is considered fully solved.

Aside from being nigh unreadable to humans, Alpöge has otherwise avoided the kinds of drama that other AI-assisted discoveries have faced in 2026.

OpenAI had to backtrack on its proof of the Navier-Stokes problem, which is another Millennium Problem, after the firm couldn’t rule out that the AI models it used had access to data from other researchers. Somewhat ironically, one of those mathematicians whose work OpenAI may have  — knowingly or unknowingly — borrowed from was Levent Alpöge, as he and others were pretty close to solving the problem on their own.

Similarly, Claude was credited with finding a new novel enzyme that humans had never seen before. The problem is that computational biologist Mario Rodríguez Mestre had seen this enzyme before and was using Claude to study it further, so it’s uncertain if Claude actually found it independently or used data from Mestre’s research to find it.

Industry observers note that the heavy assistance from AI has been met with mostly positive reactions, with most researchers agreeing that the AI usage is justified provided that the proof is proven to be true through peer review. Since no one was particularly close to solving the Riemann Hypothesis, there haven’t been any accusations of Alpöge or Claude stealing work like those prior examples. By and large, most mathematicians are excited about the discovery.

“Even before this, we have seen the power of AI, and this indicates that AI trained on hundreds of years of human mathematics can perform amazing tasks,” said Penn State’s Milewski. “I would add that AI didn’t come up with the Riemann Hypothesis, nor did most of the work to prove it, and AI probably doesn’t ‘know’ why it was invented or why it’s key.”.

In a recent development, CNET spoke with a few professors about this, and they all echoed Milewski’s sentiment, stating that AI was trained with centuries of human mathematical achievement, so a win for AI is a win for humans too. Jeffrey Lagarias, a professor of mathematics at the University of Michigan, told CNET that “I don’t think this particular proof would have been found without AI.”.

In a recent development, prasad Tetali, head of the department of mathematical sciences at Carnegie Mellon University, remarked: “It is easy to overestimate the role of AI, and underappreciate decades of human mathematician work that went into it. The AI here is really standing tall and wide on the shoulders of generations of human giants.”.

According to recent reports, on the AI side of things, influencers are attempting to use the news to hype up the capabilities of AI. Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang said in a post on X that solving the Riemann Hypothesis was a sign that AI superintelligence was close at hand and that humanity should be terrified of the “alien mind that we don’t understand.”.

AI researcher Eliezer Yudkowsky likened the whole thing to a organization making enriched uranium that’ll one day result in the end of the human species.

These warnings are hard to take seriously when one considers that Anthropic tried to make Claude solve the Riemann Hypothesis by itself back in August. Claude came up with some cool ideas but ultimately failed to solve the problem alone. For the time being, AI still needs a great deal of human guidance to make these massive discoveries, so the doom-and-gloom proselytizing comes off as a little premature.

To make things even more interesting, a competing Riemann Hypothesis proof was submitted by Alessandro Masullo just a few hours after Alpöge released his. This competing proof is 940 pages long, which is significantly shorter than Alpöge’s proof, and it was an all-human effort with no AI assistance. The proof is months in the making, with Masullo working with mathematician Brian Conrad to bring it up to spec before it hits peer review. When Alpöge posted his proof, Masullo and others thought it wise to submit theirs as well.

This started a “dueling proofs” storyline over the weekend, but it was short-lived. Shortly after Masullo’s proof was posted, multiple people found the types of flaws and omissions that often disprove Riemann Hypothesis proofs. Those complications are in the process of being corrected, and the proof is officially in mid-revision status.

Masullo kept the original proof posted (PDF) in its unedited form, but acknowledges that the proof was rushed to publication so that it could compete with Alpöge and Claude.

“The PDF below was posted on Nov. 20 on Ravi Vakil’s blog,” Masullo wrote on a Google site. “It was never meant to be shared publicly at this stage, and it has been posted in this draft form in response to current circumstances.”.

It’s entirely possible that future revisions of Masullo’s work may solve the problems in the early draft and create a fully human proof of the Riemann Hypothesis without AI, but that isn’t happening anytime soon.

Industry observers note that this is a lot of information about finding the Riemann Hypothesis, so it’s probably a good idea to briefly explain what it even is. In the 1730s, famous mathematician Leonhard Euler came up with a zeta function as a way to solve the Basel Problem, another mathematical curiosity about the exact sum of the reciprocals of squares. Euler was successful in this endeavor, and the zeta function became a part of mathematics.

Bernhard Riemann picked up where Euler left off and expanded the zeta function to use complex numbers — real numbers mixed with imaginary numbers — using a process called analytic continuation. Riemann used this expanded function to express how many prime numbers there were under a specific number and how tightly those prime numbers were packed together.

This is easy enough to do in your head with small numbers, like figuring out there are four prime numbers under 10, but when the biggest prime number is 41,024,320 digits long, having a function to do it for you is a lot more helpful.

The mechanics of Riemann’s expanded zeta function are quite complicated, and the math-focused YouTube channel Numberphile has an excellent explainer from a professional mathematician (with pictures) if you want to learn more.

The hypothesis concerns the solutions the function yields. Riemann’s version of the zeta function revealed that if you plugged in an even negative number, like -2, -4 or -672, the function would always spit out a zero. These are referred to as trivial zeroes, and Riemann proved that this was always true in his original paper.

The Riemann Hypothesis is the conjecture that all the other numbers that would also make a zero — referred to as non-trivial zeroes — follow a very specific formula, which is “½ + it”, where “i” is an imaginary number and “t” is any real number, positive or negative. In short, Riemann believed that there was no other way to generate a zero with his zeta function other than even negative numbers (trivial zeroes) and numbers that followed the “½+it” formula (non-trivial zeroes). Riemann provided some examples of the hypothesis being right but never wrote a full proof of it.

Sources indicate that it’s worth noting that not every number that follows the “½+it” formula produces a zero, but that all the numbers that produce a zero will use that formula. It’s kind of the same as saying that all squares are rectangles but not all rectangles are squares.

In the 167 years since the hypothesis was first published, mathematicians have found 12 trillion non-trivial zeroes, and every single one of them fits the above rules. Trillions of other numbers that don’t follow those rules have been tested to find a counterexample, since even one counterexample disproves the hypothesis immediately. Those efforts have produced no counterexamples at all.

This isn’t conclusive proof, but it’s such an overwhelming amount of evidence that mathematicians began assuming that the hypothesis was true, even if no one could prove it. Alpöge’s AI-assisted proof is the first to show in any context that the hypothesis is always true, which, according to Tetali, has implications in prime number understanding, number theory and other branches of mathematics.

“The big job on the math side is to find a human-understandable proof,” Lagarias said. “I would say this is certainly going to happen; there will be such understanding. Already there are several AI digests of the proof breaking it into its component pieces. I have seen one [that’s] 11 pages, 164 pages, 273 pages. There are great ideas to extract from them.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 27, 2026 at 6:05AM EST.

You've probably got a lot on your mind with the holidays in full swing, but with only a few weeks to go until 2027, it's worth taking a few minutes to map out your priorities for next year, including your retirement savings goals.

According to recent reports, goals like maxing out your IRA or contributing a certain dollar amount to your retirement account each month are great. But if you have a 401(k), there's one goal that is worth putting above all others.

In a recent development, claiming your full 401(k) match should be your top priority in 2027, unless doing so would leave you unable to pay your bills today. This match, which could be worth hundreds to thousands of dollars today, could easily grow into tens of thousands of dollars by retirement. That could be enough to cover several months of living expenses in the future.

According to recent reports, but you only get those dollars if you first contribute money to your own 401(k). Fail to do this by the end of the year, and you miss out on the opportunity to earn that money.

Given the limited time available, it's worth focusing on your 401(k) contributions first, at least until you've claimed your full match for the year. Then, if you'd like, you can switch to funding a different retirement account, such as an IRA, which offers greater flexibility.

In a recent development, what you need to do to claim your full 401(k) match in 2027 depends in part on how your firm's matching formula works. Most formulas either give you $1 or $0.50 for every dollar you put into your 401(k), up to a certain percentage of your income. For example, if you get a dollar-for-dollar match on up to 4% of your income and you earn $60,000, you'd save $2,400 of your own money and your employer would give you another $2,400.

Check with your employer to learn how its matching formula works. Then, calculate how much of your own money you must set aside to get the entire match. Divide this amount by the number of pay periods in the year to determine how much you must set aside per paycheck to get the entire match.

If you're not able to set aside the entire amount each month due to budget constraints, get as much of your match as possible. And if you get a raise later in the year, recalculate how much you need to save to get the full match and increase your contribution rate accordingly if you can.
