Black Friday Porch Pirates Don’t Care About Your Doorbell Camera. Follow This Expert Plan Now

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1238 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Doorbell cameras may seem like a good way to make a porch thief think twice, but the reality doesn’t quite match up.
  • Recent findings suggest that that’s the case for my fellow CNET editor, Gael Cooper, who had her Amazon delivery stolen a few weeks ago and spotted the thief on camera.
  • Industry observers note that “When Amazon emailed me that the order was delivered and it wasn’t there, I was very confused,” Cooper said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Doorbell cameras may seem like a good way to make a porch thief think twice, but the reality doesn’t quite match up. Some porch pirates don’t care about being caught on camera as long as they’re able to steal your package, and it’s unlikely that law enforcement will track down the stolen goods.

Recent findings suggest that that’s the case for my fellow CNET editor, Gael Cooper, who had her Amazon delivery stolen a few weeks ago and spotted the thief on camera. It wasn’t expensive tech or a snazzy holiday gift — it was $36 worth of soda.

Industry observers note that “When Amazon emailed me that the order was delivered and it wasn’t there, I was very confused,” Cooper said. “When I pulled up the Ring footage, I saw the delivery happen on video, but then, 10 minutes later, a man in a blue hooded coat who’s intentionally hiding his face reveals up and grabs the box.”.

Sources indicate that package theft cases like this happen year-round, with CNET findings showing that 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or have stopped an attempted theft. And experts predict more stolen packages during the holidays, when thieves expect more deliveries.

It has been revealed that so, don’t give thieves a chance. Now’s the time to make a blueprint to keep your Black Friday and Cyber Monday packages out of sight. But what tactics actually work if doorbell cameras don’t? Here’s what you should know about porch piracy and how to lessen your chances of package theft.

Industry observers note that cooper’s Amazon order was scheduled to arrive between 3 a.m. and 6 a.m. — when it’s dark, but she knew she would be home. But thieves were already out lurking during those hours. Cooper mentioned the thief followed the driver and stole the package. She saw the thief stealing the package on her Ring security camera system.

Greg Zakowicz, Omnisend’s e-commerce and retail advisor, remarked Cooper’s package-theft incident is fairly typical, unfortunately — especially during the holiday season.

“Thieves know as well as shoppers that orders increase during this time, and often, the packages are more likely to contain more valuable items,” said Zakowicz. “Shoppers during this time look to take advantage of deep discounts for not only gifts but themselves, making the package a potential goldmine for thieves.”.

There are a few steps you can take to lessen the likelihood of porch piracy. Zakowicz recommends using options like in-store pickups, post office boxes, in-garage delivery or deliveries to your workplace.

That advice is especially important for expensive tech you initiative to have delivered to your home unless someone will be there to grab the package immediately.

“While it may be less convenient, it’s a small price to pay to not have the hassle of gifts and expensive items going missing at the busiest shopping time of the year,” mentioned Zackowicz.

Recent findings suggest that also ask your retailers not to ship the item in the manufacturer’s packaging. Some retailers, like Amazon and Target, will clearly display this before shipping because it could be an easy hint for thieves to guess what it is — especially if it’s tech. Even though this won’t stop porch pirates from being curious about what’s in the box, it may make them think about the effort and risk versus the potential reward, Zakowicz stated.

If you want another option to have packages delivered to your home, consider scheduling your deliveries for a time you know you’ll be available. For instance, you can set up an Amazon Day to have all of your Amazon packages delivered at once so you can blueprint accordingly.

CNET found that US adults have mixed feelings about how effectively security cameras deter porch pirates: 11% of US adults believe they don’t deter them, while 9% use security cameras to get proof — not prevent it.

Industry observers note that regardless of your home security measures, don’t assume you’re safe from porch pirates just because you have a doorbell camera, and don’t use it as a means of keeping an eye on your package if you’re busy or not home. Instead, when you see motion detection, that’s a sign to grab it right away.

“The most common misunderstanding is that having security cameras will prevent thieves from stealing packages,” stated Zakowicz. “Thieves are thieves because being caught is not their biggest worry. They also know porch piracy is not at the top of most officers’ day-to-day public service worries. Often, by the time the report is made, thieves are long gone.”.

Unfortunately, thieves may find other ways to steal packages, since their tactics are constantly changing. If that happens to you, there are a few steps you should take right away.

It has been revealed that file a police report of the incident first. Be prepared to share information, including a description of the thief, and the make and model of the vehicle, with the police and your community so they can be vigilant of the thief.

Sources indicate that but don’t get your hopes up that the thief will be caught. Zakowicz stated it’s rare that porch theft cases get solved.

“Police aren’t necessarily dedicating resources to solving porch pirates who stole a fresh stuffed animal or board game. However, it’s key for them to understand areas seeing an uptick in thefts, as they can be more alert to suspicious activity,” remarked Zakowicz. And the retailer may request it.

After filing, Zakowicz indicates to report the theft to the carrier and retailer. Carriers may use the data to assess future likelihood of package theft incidents and it could help instruct delivery drivers to carefully hide packages. Retailers may also be able to assist with a replacement.

Cooper filed a police report with her local police department, which allowed her to upload the Ring video of the theft and acknowledged receipt. She’s not expecting the thief to be caught, but figures that her report could possibly help in some way.

“I live in a pretty safe neighborhood in Amazon’s own hometown, but their delivery trucks are on our street dropping off packages every day,” she noted. “It’s got to be a banquet for hungry thieves.”.

She reached out to her neighbors to tell them about the theft, and one reported that she, too, had had a package stolen a week earlier.

Industry observers note that cooper claims she did not intentionally choose the early-morning drop-off time, but it was the only time Amazon offered for her delivery. Since then, she’s seen Amazon try to offer that same time and has chosen not to order an item rather than be forced to use that dark, quiet delivery slot.

Recent findings suggest that immediately after the theft, Amazon was less than helpful, routing her to an AI agent who noted it understood the situation was upsetting but that it wouldn’t be able to do anything for four days. When she checked back, Amazon agreed to refund her for the item, but kept insisting on labeling the package as “missing” and asked her to report back if she “found” it.

“I hope the driver doesn’t get in trouble for a supposedly ‘missing’ package,” she noted. “It unnerves me that she was being followed by a thief. Who knows how long he followed that truck and how many packages he scooped up?”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer.
  • Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.
  • Anthropic first released artifacts in 2024.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer. The “install as app” feature is available in beta for all free and paid Claude plans and works on both Mac and Windows, but not Linux.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Anthropic first released artifacts in 2024. Since then, they’ve become a way to standardize and repeat tasks customers do regularly, especially at work. Previously, artifacts ran via your Claude window or in a browser. By splicing them out as distinct desktop apps, you can now run different Claude queries while also using your artifacts locally, or use those apps without opening Claude at all.

In a recent development, “When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer,” Anthropic said.

Artifact apps can still access Claude and any connectors you’re using, and they enhancement automatically when you edit the artifact itself in Claude. When apps request something from Claude, though, that goes toward your Claude usage limits, which are lowest for free owners.

Anthropic stated the app feature is meant to streamline building apps for both developer and non-developer work.

According to recent reports, also: Can AI initiative terrorist attacks? US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok.

Industry observers note that the update clarifies where AI software for work is headed. Claude is already more of an AI-powered work suite than a single helpful chatbot for many organizations. Evidently, people are using tools like artifacts frequently enough — and simultaneously with other Claude features — that they need those Claude-based tools to function like discrete bits of software on their own.

“If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” Anthropic noted.

Industry observers note that claude artifact apps don’t have the same functionality as apps you could build using Claude Code, though. Even if you don’t need Claude open for these apps to work, you’ll still need to be signed in to Claude and have internet access, so they’re not an entirely portable or off-grid option.

The feature’s support page also notes that legacy artifacts, “live artifacts from Claude Cowork,” and artifacts generated from templates like Docs, Slides, and Sheets can’t be installed as desktop apps.

First, make sure Claude for Mac or Windows is updated. You can try the “install as app” feature, which is in beta for all free and paid intends, via Claude’s Share menu. Select the Install as app option, which will then download the artifact you chose to your desktop. From there, set permissions as needed.

Permissions range from the default (whatever they are in a browser) to app-specific permissions like sending notifications and full computer access.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free.

Full computer access means the artifact app can “run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time,” Anthropic noted, so proceed carefully. Every time you edit and update the artifact (and thus the app), Claude will ask you to confirm permissions again, so you’ll ideally have regular checkpoints to revise access. Still, there are some guardrails in place: Anthropic only lets you give full computer access to apps you’ve made yourself. For Team and Enterprise plans, that extends to any apps made by your coworkers.

“Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust,” the company mentioned.

For Claude Enterprise aims, the install-as-app feature is off entirely until an admin turns it on in Organization settings.

4 Security Devices I Rely On for Front Porch and Delivery Protection

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason.
  • From protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without.
  • Old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest and greatest home security products often start at your front door, and for good reason. That’s where burglars first try, too, and research reveals thieves can be deterred with the presence of a security cam — but security technology can do so much more.

From protecting packages to managing access the smart way, here are the devices I use every day to guard my front door, and I couldn’t imagine my home without. Take a look to see what your porch could use, too, and the tech options I recommend looking at.

Old deadbolts do well, but any entryway can get a powerful upgrade by adding digital features via a smart lock. Smart locks allow you to control your front door lock from anywhere using your phone, as well as creating temporary passes for guests. They can support digital wallet keys for touchless unlocking, and many have keypads or fingerprint readers. Plus, you can enable settings like auto-locking, so you never have to worry about forgetting to lock the door.

Smart locks come in two flavors: retrofits that leave your deadbolt largely intact and only replace your indoor thumb turn, and full deadbolt replacements that give you latest locking power, inside and out. Don’t worry about installation: If you’ve never installed a deadbolt before, the process is generally easy and doesn’t take much time. I have a full guide where you can find more details.

According to recent reports, say goodbye to dusty doorbells of the past. Today’s high-tech doorbells do far more than chime: Video doorbells keep an eye on your front porch, while also giving you a two-way audio intercom right on your phone to hold a conversation — or even let an LLM do the talking for you.

It has been revealed that video doorbells also have particularly useful object recognition features, sometimes even for free. That includes recognizing packages and alerting you whenever one highlights up at your door, or when one suddenly vanishes. Video storage options can save recordings of key events, so you can check who came to the door if you need to.

These advanced doorbells come in both wired and wireless versions. I’m a fan of the battery-powered, wireless models, which you can set and angle to get just the right look at your porch, doormat and other key places. Many can also work with your current door chime, although you probably don’t need it anymore with phone-based chimes.

Yale’s delivery boxes are larger, so you need room for them in the right spots.

Recent findings suggest that package theft concerns have reignited a centuries-old tradition of protecting mail. Today’s modern delivery boxes are specifically designed to allow delivery people to put packages inside, but make it difficult or impossible for thieves to take packages out, through clever lock models, auto-locking, smart controls and other various tricks.

I’ve been using a delivery box myself for a couple of years and find it very handy, as long as you have the space by your door. Some versions even come weighted or screwed down if you’re worried about a porch pirate absconding with the entire box. It’s a good idea to put notes in your deliveries to use the box, since despite signs not all delivery people will notice it’s there.

As a final plus, these boxes also keep your packages protected from the elements, which is nice when you live in an area that gets frequent winter snowstorms, as I do.

Smart bulbs are cheap, support multiple voice assistants and have lots of fun tricks.

Sources indicate that where front doors exist, there’s usually a light nearby, like an overhead porch light or a wall-mounted lamp, to illuminate the entryway and surrounding area. These lights can also get a major makeover if you switch to an LED smart bulb, which are available as both BR30 floodlights and standard A19 home bulbs.

It has been revealed that these lights also give you phone app controls, which is more key than it might seem. With my apps, I can control brightness, set schedules for bulbs to turn on or off, and even adjust the color to whatever I want, say for a holiday event. All it takes is screwing in the bulb and connecting it to Wi-Fi, so you can be done in seconds.

Industry observers note that if you feel like experimenting, you can usually link smart bulbs to other devices, too. For example, you could set the light to turn on automatically when a smart lock is unlocked, or when a security system is disarmed.

Now that your front porch is up to date, take a look at the latest home AI tricks I’ve found are actually worth using and how to get them.

At $640 off, it’s worth considering if you’re looking for a compact scooter with some serious power.

Sources indicate that the Vmax VX2 Lite is another scooter on my review list. It’s a more affordable alternative to the Hub, and at $460 off, it could be worth checking out if you don’t need the Hub’s additional performance. I’ll have more to share once I’ve had a chance to test it.

Sources indicate that the Inmotion V9 is one of the more beginner-friendly electric unicycles I’ve reviewed. It has built-in cellular connectivity, allowing you to track its location if it goes missing, along with suspension for a more comfortable ride. It’s also UL 2272 certified, an crucial consideration when bringing a lithium-ion-powered ride into your home.

At $500 off, it’s an appealing option for anyone looking to get into electric unicycles without spending a fortune.

Shop Inmotion’s Black Friday deals.

If none of these models fit your needs, there are a few other sales worth checking out.

Super73 has discounts on select models, including the Z Miami Core and S2 Laguna, both priced at $1,895. Its sale runs through Dec. 2.

Velotric is offering savings of up to $700 on select e-bikes, including the Summit 1, advertised at $1,299. The Nomad 2 and folding Fold 1 Plus are also discounted.

It has been revealed that juiced Bikes has marked down several models in its Scrambler lineup for Black Friday. The Scrambler Mini starts at $949, down from $1,164, while the Scrambler Hardtail is $1,599 (save $445) and the Full Suspension is $1,799 (save $445). If you’re looking for more range, the dual-battery Hardtail is $1,899, down from $2,344.

Shop Juiced Bikes Black Friday deals.

Segway also has discounts on several other scooters, including the Max G2 for $598.48, ZT3 Pro for $790 and E3 Pro for $500.

Sources indicate that many of the manufacturers featured here have additional Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals across their product lines. I wanted to spotlight the bikes, scooters and electric unicycles we’ve had or currently have in-house because we’ve actually spent time with them. There are other products we’ve tested that could have made this list, too, but I wanted to give readers a useful selection rather than overwhelm them with every discounted model.

According to recent reports, don’t get too caught up in the discount. Make sure the bike, scooter or unicycle fits your needs, particularly when it comes to rider weight, range, portability and storage. Manufacturers’ range estimates are generally based on favorable conditions, and your actual mileage will vary depending on weight, speed, hills and temperature.

Industry observers note that apple Find My and other tracking systems can help locate a missing ride, but they’re no substitute for a good physical lock. And when it comes to battery safety, look for the appropriate UL certification, use the manufacturer-approved charger and never charge your bike or scooter where it blocks your exit.

It has been revealed that most of these deals run through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, although some promotions continue into December. Prices and availability can change.

Tech Sell-Off: 1 Unstoppable Stock-Split Stock to Buy Before It Joins Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Apple in the $3 Trillion Club

💡 Key Takeaways
  • is home to four publicly listed companies worth $3 trillion or more: Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Apple.
  • A high stock price can make it difficult for retail investors to buy into a given tech giant, unless they have access to a broker that offers fractional shares.
  • It has been revealed that meta Platforms (META +3.78%) recently unveiled a 2-for-1 split, which it will achieve by introducing a fresh class of shares.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Di Pizio – Nov 27, 2026 at 7:17AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Meta Platforms ›.

In a recent development, the U.S. is home to four publicly listed companies worth $3 trillion or more: Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Apple. Those companies have created so much long-term value that if they didn't occasionally execute stock splits, their respective share prices would be in the thousands of dollars.

A high stock price can make it difficult for retail investors to buy into a given tech giant, unless they have access to a broker that offers fractional shares. A stock split increases the number of shares in circulation, reducing the price per share by a proportionate amount. It's entirely cosmetic, so it doesn't change the value of the underlying company, but it makes the stock far more accessible for small investors.

It has been revealed that meta Platforms (META +3.78%) recently unveiled a 2-for-1 split, which it will achieve by introducing a fresh class of shares. An investor who right now owns one Meta Class A share worth $600 will soon own two shares: one Class A share (with voting rights) and one Class C share (with no voting rights), each worth $300. The split is expected to take effect sometime in January, although the official date is yet to be confirmed.

Industry observers note that meta has created tremendous value for investors since going public in 2012. Even after accounting for the steep sell-off in the broader market over the past month, the company still has a market capitalization of $1.53 trillion (as of Nov. 25). However, I think it could join the exclusive $3 trillion club within the next few years, giving investors an opportunity to nearly double their money. Here's why.

Meta is the parent firm of social media platforms Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads. During the third quarter of 2026 (ended Sept. 30), a whopping 3.64 billion people used at least one of those applications every day. That is a significant portion of the world's population, so it's getting harder for Meta to find newly introduced users, especially because its apps are banned in China, which is home to over 1.4 billion people.

That's why Meta is focusing more on engagement. If each existing user spends more time online, they will see more advertisements, and the manufacturer will make more money. Artificial intelligence (AI) is at the center of this strategy, because it helps Meta's recommendation algorithms learn what type of content each user likes to see, so it can show them more of it. The company's chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg, said engagement on Facebook and Instagram hit record highs in the third quarter, so the approach is working.

NASDAQ · As of 10:40 AM ET 11/27/26.

But thanks to AI, Meta is also penetrating entirely new markets outside of social media. The firm introduced a personal AI agent called Muse in September, and it already has over 10 million customers. It can perform a range of tasks, but Zuckerberg indicates one-third of users have deployed it as a personal shopper, with an average purchase size of $200.

Zuckerberg thinks Muse could eventually help billions of people improve their lives, whether they want business advice or tips for healthy living. This will expand Meta's addressable opportunity by potentially taking traffic away from traditional internet search engines like Google Search.

According to Wall Street's average estimate (provided by Yahoo Finance), Meta is on track to generate $256.9 billion in revenue this year, representing a 27% increase from 2025. Most of that will come from selling ads to businesses on Facebook and Instagram, but Muse gives Meta an opportunity to make money from subscriptions and also transaction fees when the assistant makes purchases. So, it could make a major contribution to the manufacturer's revenue in the future.

Meta generated earnings of $29.33 per share over the last four quarters, placing its stock at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 20.1. That is a steep discount to the P/E ratio of the Nasdaq-100 index, which is 27.4, suggesting Meta is heavily undervalued compared to a group of America's largest tech companies.

Moreover, Wall Street predicts Meta will grow its earnings to $33.74 per share in 2027, placing its stock at a forward P/E ratio of 16.6.

Assuming Wall Street's earnings forecast holds up, Meta stock would have to soar by 64% by the end of next year just to trade in line with the P/E ratio of the Nasdaq-100, which is certainly possible considering its P/E was above 30 for a large portion of the last decade.

That gain alone would see Meta's market cap rise to $2.51 trillion, so earnings growth of 19.5% in 2028 would be enough to catapult the organization into the $3 trillion club. Alternatively, earnings growth of just 9.5% in both 2028 and 2029 would produce the same result.

I say that because slower earnings growth is a real possibility given how much money Meta is spending on AI data centers. It spent $72 billion in 2025 and is on track to spend up to $145 billion in 2026. The firm can't deduct these costs up front because AI infrastructure has a useful life of several years, so it must be depreciated over time instead. That means every dollar spent today could impact Meta's earnings in 2028, 2029, and even 2030.

Nevertheless, I think Meta has a very high chance of joining the $3 trillion club at some point, even if it takes a little more time than I've outlined.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, we don’t usually see companies announcing brand-new products just before Black Friday sales kick off, but after spending a day playing with Kodak’s new SlideTag, I’m sure glad it’s available now, because this is what most of my family is getting as a gift this year. Strictly speaking, it’s not even discounted, but its already cheap $35 price tag means this is just too good to pass up.

According to recent reports, the SlideTag is a tiny digital photo frame that sits on a keychain, but it’s also a tracker compatible with both Apple’s Find My and Google’s Find Hub. You can load it up with photos and have the six-color E-Ink display cycle through them at set intervals, or you can put something more practical on the screen.

The Kodak app makes it easy to generate a QR code, display a to-do list, countdown to a special event or just show you the current date in a nice calendar display. It’s incredibly easy to use, the color E-Ink display is surprisingly good and setting up the tracking feature is super easy. This thing does exactly what it notes it does, and with very little learning curve.

So what’s the catch? You don’t really get to choose what the outside of your SlideTag looks like. These clever little photo frames are only available as a blind box, showcasing eight designs across the vibrant history of Kodak’s packaging and something Kodak calls a secret edition, which is unique to this set.

Recent findings suggest that I ordered two, and while both designs I found in the packaging are great, there are other designs in the lineup I’d have chosen first. Some retailers are selling cases of eight SlideTags with promotional packaging, like you’d see at the checkout counter of a grocery store, but this case doesn’t guarantee you’re going to get all eight designs. There’s no real way to know what you’re going to get.

Industry observers note that that level of risk may not be your thing, but if you’re looking for a way to add a stealthy little tracker with no shortage of personality to your bag, backpack or purse, I think this is a great option. It also makes a great little gift, perfect for a stocking or white elephant party. And if this level of cutesy fun isn’t your thing, Apple’s second-gen AirTags are on sale for $18 this week.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 25, 2026, FinVolution (FINV -3.91%) revealed a sharp contraction in domestic loan volume as management prioritized credit quality over origination growth. The retreat in Chinese lending tests whether international expansion can protect profitability during a home-market regulatory reset. Three things management mentioned stand out.

Industry observers note that china's domestic loan volume dropped sharply after tighter collection rules and risk-averse bank partners constrained credit. FinVolution relied on its international operations to pick up the slack as overseas revenue climbed 11% year over year.

According to recent reports, management shrank domestic origination instead of writing risky loans during an industrywide funding squeeze. Tighter underwriting models now filter out high-risk applicants and allocate credit to proven borrowers.

FinVolution integrated open banking, a system that shares verified financial data with customer consent, to assess borrowers' income and debt. That data allowed the firm to concern larger loans in Australia without loosening risk standards.

Regulatory resets and institutional funding pullbacks across China are pressuring the industry. FinVolution holds RMB 8.4 billion in cash and short-term investments to navigate the turbulence.

Sources indicate that financial stability rests on a historical low leverage ratio, calculated as risk-bearing loan balance divided by equity, of 1.5 times. Management continues to prioritize loan quality heading into the fourth quarter.

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.
  • The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.
  • During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

Industry observers note that newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

Newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

Industry observers note that the North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059.

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

In a recent development, elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

Sources indicate that the striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Sources indicate that woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

Industry observers note that play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Recent findings suggest that time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

According to recent reports, leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Sources indicate that good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

In a recent development, bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

It has been revealed that corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

In a recent development, the scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

In a recent development, newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

According to recent reports, lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

Good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

On the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a significant threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

Fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Newcastle get the game under way.

In a recent development, matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane.

Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two fresh credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

It has been revealed that the two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

According to recent reports, they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

According to recent reports, 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

It has been revealed that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

Recent findings suggest that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for latest applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

Recent findings suggest that 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

In a recent development, 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

It has been revealed that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

Recent findings suggest that to maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

Travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

It has been revealed that the card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

Industry observers note that with the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in Upcoming York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

Recent findings suggest that bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

However, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

Recent findings suggest that the earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

Industry observers note that plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

Industry observers note that those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

One of the most interesting perks of the newly introduced cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

There are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
  • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
  • It has been revealed that A visual exterior inspection.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

It has been revealed that A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

An interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any complications are documented.

According to recent reports, A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

Sources indicate that service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic challenges that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

In a recent development, inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

Industry observers note that detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

Recent findings suggest that reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

The good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

However, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

Some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

It has been revealed that some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

Reddit is an online forum where owners share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

Reddit consumers are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

According to recent reports, car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several customers suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

    Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

    Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

    United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

    United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

    #155225. What Are Repositioning Cruises?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1022 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    What Are Repositioning Cruises?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1022 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
    • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
    • Industry observers note that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

    Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

    Industry observers note that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

    Industry observers note that one key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

    This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

    Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

    Just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a new region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

    Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit important sites when off the ship.

    If there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

    For ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy demonstrates, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

    Many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

    If you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

    You can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

    Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

    Here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

    This journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

    Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between Newly introduced York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

    Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

    In a recent development, departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

    If Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and New England before reaching the Big Apple.

    Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching New York.

    Sources indicate that unitedHealth Group (UNH +1.33%) recently upgraded its yearly earnings guidance for the third time this year. In each of its quarterly earnings reports, its expectations for yearly adjusted earnings per share (EPS) have climbed.

    According to recent reports, in its 2025 annual report, the healthcare insurer had 2026 adjusted EPS of at least $17.75. After the first quarter, it said it would be at least $18.25. The second quarter brought another increase to between $19.50 and $20. Now, after the third quarter, UnitedHealth Group is predicting full-year EPS of at least $20.50.

    In the meantime, though, the stock has climbed only 3%. So far this month, its shares are down more than 18%. That's because of a rising chorus from both sides of the political aisle that something must be done to rein in Medicare Advantage costs, and because of the possibility that Medicare-for-all proposals, if they became law, would upend the company's business model.

    According to recent reports, on Nov. 16, a proposed rule, called CRUSH, from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), was floated to curb healthcare fraud. This heightened concerns about increased expenses and potential repayment liabilities for Medicare Advantage providers such as UnitedHealth Group. The rule would increase audits of insurance providers and allow CMS to recover improper payments.

    The current dip for UnitedHealth Group presents an opportunity and a question: What would a $10,000 investment return if the company's turnaround continues?

    If you had invested $10,000 in UnitedHealth Group stock 10 years ago and reinvested its dividends, you would have around $26,600 today, representing an annual return of 10.3%. Over the next 10 years, it's possible the stock could deliver an annual return of more than 10%. Let's make the case for why that could happen.

    NYSE · As of 10:34 AM ET 11/27/26.

    The stock is trading at around 19 times trailing earnings, well below its historical valuation of about 22 times earnings.

    After a couple of down years, the company appears to be in the midst of a turnaround. It saw quarterly EPS rise by 76.21% year over year in Q3 and by 61.72% in Q2. It has been able to do that because management's margin-over-volume strategy of exiting unprofitable geographies, tightening benefits, and shifting Medicare Advantage mix toward higher-margin Special Needs Aims (SNPs) is successfully restoring core insurance margins.

    In a recent development, in Q3, UnitedHealth Group reported that revenue declined year over year by 0.09% to $86.3 billion. However, net income rose to $2.8 billion, up from $1.8 billion in the same period a year ago, and nine-month operating margin rose from 5.6% to 7%.

    In a recent development, most headline-grabbing CMS rules are proposed regulations subject to public comment periods, revisions, and multi-year phase-ins rather than instant earnings hits. For example, key provider enrollment provisions under the CRUSH proposal would not take effect until the plan year beginning two years after a final rule is published.

    Plus, UnitedHealthcare prepares reprice annually, allowing the firm to adapt to changes. If CMS reduces benchmark reimbursements or tightens quality bonus thresholds, UnitedHealthcare adjusts by trimming supplemental benefits (such as dental, vision, or over-the-counter allowances), raising deductibles, or narrowing provider networks, as it did for its 2027 bids to protect its 2% to 4% Medicare Advantage operating margin target.

    Heavy compliance burdens, stricter risk-adjustment documentation rules, and narrower margins disproportionately squeeze smaller regional insurers and start-up prepares that lack massive actuarial, legal, and data infrastructure.

    When tighter rules force smaller competitors to exit unprofitable counties or slash benefits, UnitedHealth's unmatched scale allows it to absorb compliance costs and capture displaced market share over time.

    Sources indicate that even if Medicare Advantage faces strict federal scrutiny, UnitedHealth Group is not a pure-play Medicare Advantage insurer. Its earnings are heavily cushioned by Optum (Optum Rx, Optum Health, and Optum Insight) and by its massive commercial employer-sponsored insurance book, insulating overall enterprise earnings from single-program rule changes.

    The company raised its quarterly dividend by just under 5% this year to $2.32 per share, the 17th consecutive year it has increased its dividend. The dividend yield is an above-average 2.65%.

    If UnitedHealth Group can sustain double-digit EPS growth, the stock would likely grow by 12% to 15% each year. Counting the company's dividend, it wouldn't be unreasonable for a $10,000 investment now to be worth at least $31,058 a decade from now.

    The tech giant has faced challenges to its business models before, but its size and scope give it the ability to overcome legal challenges that could affect its bottom line, potentially widening its moat against competitors.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Another day, another substantial swing.
    • Industry observers note that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
    • In a recent development, the amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Another day, another substantial swing. This one's lower, but don't count on it starting a trend: We keep seeing mortgage rates move back and forth, but no one's expecting rates to take a dive. If you're watching this space because you're waiting to refinance, it's unlikely your wait is about to end.

    Industry observers note that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points lower than yesterday and unchanged from a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    In a recent development, the amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising. Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.).

    Industry observers note that my point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    According to recent reports, mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to fresh inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

    Sources indicate that strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

    We already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three substantial inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI showed wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

    According to recent reports, predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Recent findings suggest that markets are currently anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

    But back to the upcoming holiday: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

    » Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you strategy to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

    Industry observers note that also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    It has been revealed that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    In a recent development, if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    Industry observers note that 🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

    » Stay informed: Check out NerdWallet's mortgage news hub for all our latest coverage.

    In a recent development, the rate you see advertised is a sample rate — usually for a borrower with perfect credit, making a big down payment, and paying for mortgage points. That won't match every buyer's circumstances.

    Even two people with similar credit scores might get different rates, depending on their overall financial profiles.

    Tech Report: Is Nvidia a Screaming Buy or a Value Trap?
