    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -0.89%) stock has raced higher during most of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, and this is thanks to the company's leading position in the space.
    • All of this has driven significant revenue growth, with numbers reaching record levels time and time again.
    • According to recent reports, you might expect such a stock to be expensive, but Nvidia, due to recent headwinds, has actually seen its valuation tumble to record lows.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adria Cimino – Nov 27, 2026 at 8:05AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -0.89%) stock has raced higher during most of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, and this is thanks to the company's leading position in the space. The tech giant makes the world's fastest graphics processing units (GPUs), the chips powering key AI tasks. And over the past few years, it's greatly expanded its portfolio to include a wide variety of related products and services.

    All of this has driven significant revenue growth, with numbers reaching record levels time and time again. This continued in the third quarter, as revenue jumped more than 100% to $115 billion and the company generated high profitability on sales with a gross margin of more than 74%.

    According to recent reports, you might expect such a stock to be expensive, but Nvidia, due to recent headwinds, has actually seen its valuation tumble to record lows. At today's levels, is Nvidia a screaming buy or a value trap? Let's find out.

    First, you might wonder how high-growth Nvidia could today have a valuation that puts it in the category of "value stock." Nvidia trades for only 16x forward earnings estimates, a historically low level for this tech player.

    NVDA PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

    A few elements have contributed to this. Throughout this year, investors have worried about substantial tech companies' spending levels as they lead the AI infrastructure build-out. Players such as Amazon and Alphabet, for example, are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on data centers, chips, and more to serve AI demand. But investors question whether this enormous investment will match the future revenue opportunity. This has hurt AI stocks at times in 2026, and broader economic concerns amid rising inflation have also proved challenging.

    To make matters worse, just recently, reports emerged that Nvidia chief Jensen Huang allegedly had affairs with at least two women -- one called a Chinese spy by U.S. intelligence agents and the other an Nvidia executive. Huang stepped down, and the stock plummeted. Nvidia's board reinstated him days later, and the stock rebounded, but it continues to trade at a dirt cheap valuation.

    In a recent development, now, let's consider our question: Is Nvidia a screaming buy or a value trap? For a stock to be a value trap, the firm must have a significant amount of underlying trouble that is putting pressure on or will put pressure on earnings. This could be declining market share or a sustained drop in revenue, for example.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia isn't in this situation. To the contrary, business is booming. In the latest quarter, revenue and profit advanced in the triple digits to record levels, and the tech giant's rollout of its latest platform, Vera Rubin, met with soaring demand. Meanwhile, Nvidia's multi-year road map and its commitment to innovation offer us reason to be confident in its competitive position.

    So, the stock isn't a value trap. Instead, it's declined due to the headwinds I mentioned above -- and the pressure remains. Some investors continue to worry about AI spending, and any slowdown in such spending could impact the revenue growth of Nvidia and peers.

    Nvidia-specific troubles also remain in the background. The company's board is investigating Huang's interactions with the woman whom intelligence agents consider a spy. Separately, Huang must testify before Congressional panels early next month on the matter. Meanwhile, the press also reported recently that regulators are investigating Nvidia's accounting practices. All of these elements could weigh on stock performance in the weeks and months to come.

    Sources indicate that now, we know Nvidia isn't a value trap -- but is it a screaming buy? It's clear that the stock looks like a bargain today considering the firm's earnings track record and potential earnings down the road. That remarked, any negative news stemming from the headwinds I mentioned above could slow Nvidia's growth story at least temporarily. Amid the uncertainty, Nvidia isn't the best bet for a cautious investor today, and this uncertainty means that it isn't yet a "screaming" buy. But for a growth investor who doesn't mind these risks or potential volatility ahead, now is a great time to scoop up at least a few Nvidia shares.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a organization's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The firm has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    According to recent reports, in an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the tech giant's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    Specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in newly introduced wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

    Recent findings suggest that mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

    Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the tech giant to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

    In a recent development, the 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

    Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

    "As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," stated Mackay.

    It has been revealed that mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent confirmed an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

    Heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from fresh shares.

    "CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," said Richardson.

    Industry observers note that the 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

    Latest Update: How to Get Grants for College

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education.
    • Grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses.
    • Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education. It’s free money you aren’t expected to pay back.

    Grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses. Some grants, depending on who awards them, require an application or have requirements you must meet before you can get your money.

    Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.

    There are four main types of grants:.

    Federal grants come from the federal government.

    State grants come from state programs and often can only be used at schools in that state.

    Institutional grants come from your college or university, or even your program or major.

    Private grants come from nonprofits, community organizations and individual donors.

    To receive a federal grant, you must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Most states require the FAFSA for state grants, and a few require a separate state application. You’ll need to complete the FAFSA for each year you’re enrolled in school. You may need to meet certain eligibility requirements, such as income limits, to get some grants. The FAFSA is how you apply for the Pell Grant, which is a financial need-based grant. The FAFSA also determines eligibility for federal work-study, which is a job program rather than a grant.

    Federal aid, including federal grants, typically requires students to meet satisfactory academic progress. This means you have to maintain a minimum grade point average and be on track to finish your degree on time, as determined by your school. Your school also sets how many credits you must take to qualify for grant funding.

    Recent findings suggest that some grants — typically private or institutional grants — require an additional application that asks for transcripts, letters of recommendation and personal essays. Your school’s financial aid office or the grant provider will have details on applying for specific grants.

    After you submit the FAFSA, you’ll receive a financial aid award letter from each school you applied to, which outlines how much in federal, state and institutional grants you’ve been offered. You must accept your aid to receive it.

    In a recent development, most grants will be disbursed directly to your college or university. Your school will apply the grant money first to tuition, fees and any other charges it bills, such as housing or a meal plan.

    In some cases, you may receive more grant money than your school bills, which is the best-case scenario. If that happens to you, any leftover funds will likely be refunded to you. Refund timelines vary by school, so it may take some time to get your money. You can get your refund faster by setting up direct deposit with your school. You can then use the funds for other costs approved by your grant — some examples are detailed below.

    If you have questions about your grant money, contact your college’s financial aid office.

    Grants can help cover cost-of-attendance expenses. Generally, you can use grant money to pay for tuition, textbooks, class materials, transportation, housing and food. Depending on your school’s policies, you can use grant money to cover summer classes or study abroad programs, too.

    Industry observers note that some grants come with specific terms about how you can spend them. Check your financial aid award letter or, for a private or institutional grant, the school’s or organization’s website to find specifics.

    Expenses grants aren’t meant for:.

    Recent findings suggest that after your grant is applied to your tuition and school expenses, you can options to fill the gaps between what the grant covers and the total cost of your program. Some options include savings, scholarships, work-study, payment aims, federal student loans or, as a last resort, private loans. By using grants to pay for your college education, you may be able to borrow less.

    To maximize the grants you’re eligible to receive, enter accurate information on the FAFSA and complete it as soon as you can — some funds are first-come, first-served. Also, don’t limit yourself to federal or state grants — search and apply for as many privately funded grants as you can find.

    Industry observers note that your grant money usually goes straight to your college or university to pay your tuition and fees. Anything that is left over may be disbursed to you for other school-related costs.

    Industry observers note that yes, but it depends on your grant. Housing is part of your cost of attendance, so you can use grant money to pay for off-campus rent.

    You don’t have to pay back a grant as long as you continue to meet all requirements for the grant, such as staying enrolled. You can use grant money on school and school-related expenses. Some grants may require you to meet eligibility requirements such as a minimum GPA or state residency. If you receive more grant money than your cost of attendance for a given school term, ask your financial aid office if you can put that grant money toward next year’s cost of attendance.

    If you have a federal grant like a Pell Grant, these are examples when you may have to repay all or part of the grant:.

    You withdrew from your program.

    You received enough scholarship money to reduce your federal aid need.

    It depends. You can usually use grant money to buy a laptop. Computers are considered course materials, which fall under cost-of-attendance expenses, so they can be covered by a grant. However, always double-check with the grant provider and your financial aid award letter to ensure that you’re following all restrictions. Whether you can use grant money to cover a laptop depends on your school’s policies and how much grant money you receive.

    If you get more grant money than your school bills you, you’ll likely receive the leftover money to spend on other cost-of-attendance expenses. You can use this money on living costs such as transportation or housing. Grant money often goes mostly toward tuition, so a refund isn’t guaranteed.

    Grant and scholarship money is generally tax-free when you use it for tuition, required fees, books and required class supplies. If you have additional questions, consider talking to a tax professional.

    2026 has been challenging for stock market investors.     With rising interest rates and turbulence in the artificial intelligence (AI) industry casting a cloud of uncertainty over the market, being diversified heading into 2027 might be a smart strategy. The Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (VTI +1.23%) is one of the most diversified exchange-traded funds (ETFs) money can buy, because it tracks the Morningstar U.S. Total Market index, which holds all 3,463 companies listed on American stock exchanges.

    It has been revealed that that means the ETF has exposure to tech giants like Nvidia and Amazon, alongside small-cap growth stocks like DigitalOcean and Duolingo. Here's why it could be a great buy for the latest year.

    It has been revealed that the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF is weighted by market capitalization, meaning the most valuable companies in the fund have a much greater influence over its performance than the least valuable. Therefore, its top five holdings also happen to be the largest companies in the U.S. (and the world): Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet.

    Those five companies have a combined market cap of $18.7 trillion, so they represent 25.9% of the value of the Vanguard ETF's entire portfolio. That sounds like a very high weighting for an ETF that holds almost 3,500 different stocks, but those five giants have even bigger weightings of 29.2% in the S&P 500 and 50.1% in the Nasdaq-100.

    Its lesser exposure to those tech powerhouses is the primary reason why the Vanguard ETF typically underperforms the S&P and Nasdaq-100 over the long term.

    In a recent development, however, its high level of diversification also means the Vanguard ETF tends to suffer shallower declines during volatile periods. For example, while the Nasdaq-100 was recently down by as much as 20% from its peak, the Vanguard ETF was down by just 11.5% at its lowest point.

    There is another benefit to being highly diversified. The Vanguard ETF gives investors exposure to thousands of small- and mid-cap companies that aren't present in the major indexes. Here are some examples:.

    The Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF has delivered a compound annual return of 9.4% since it was established in 2001. However, thanks to the incredible growth in the technology sector, it has delivered a much faster annual return of 23.1% over the last three years.

    Recent findings suggest that therefore, while its long-term returns tend to be relatively modest, the ETF is certainly capable of delivering accelerated gains in certain conditions. But even if we assume the fund delivers a compound annual return of just 9.4% going forward, that's still enough to help investors build life-changing wealth.

    Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
    • It has been revealed that how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
    • So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the fresh signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    It has been revealed that how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    According to recent reports, title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    Another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    In a recent development, “They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    It has been revealed that “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    Recent findings suggest that you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    Sources indicate that here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s upcoming £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

    When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

    It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

    Sources indicate that city, in contrast to their opponents, highlighted a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where latest boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

    Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

    Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

    Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    It has been revealed that had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal indicated was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

    “I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

    You would be brave to say it will be their last.

    Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

    Manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

    Referee Sam Barrott (Yorkshire).

    It has been revealed that it’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

    I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

    In a recent development, A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we showed, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

    He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

    In a recent development, I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

    The feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

    Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

    Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka.

    The players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

    Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7.

    In a recent development, what happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.

    According to recent reports, marmoush is feeling his hip after a challenge by Mosquera. City have a free-kick wide right. Gabriel heads away Grealish’s delivery in trademark fashion.

    10 stocks we like better than Diana Shipping ›.

    In a recent development, on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 25, 2026, Diana Shipping (DSX +0.22%) confirmed a dividend increase to $0.05 per share alongside $44 million in gains from selling its investment in Genco Shipping & Trading Limited. A dry bulk carrier (a merchant vessel built to transport unpackaged commodities like coal or iron ore) relies on time charter rates (daily rental contracts for shipping vessels) staying above daily cash breakeven levels to generate profit. Three things management mentioned stand out.

    Transaction expenses of $12.3 million created a Q3 net loss of $0.5 million after Diana Shipping withdrew its acquisition offer. Selling 4.2 million Genco shares generated $112 million in net proceeds.

    Management raised the quarterly cash payout fivefold to $0.05 per common share, supported by $217.5 million in cash reserves and a net loan-to-value ratio (the proportion of net debt relative to vessel market value) of 32%.

    By securing fixed charter coverage for 93% of remaining 2026 operating days at an average daily rate of $19,736, the manufacturer created a profit cushion over its daily cash breakeven cost of $16,593.

    It has been revealed that long-haul trade routes and port inefficiencies keep vessel speeds near historical lows, creating favorable supply dynamics while dry bulk demand expands. Diana Shipping maintains high fleet utilization (the proportion of days vessels are actively operating) and a staggered contract schedule to protect cash flow against potential fleet growth, while management monitors trade routing disruptions.

    Management intends to evaluate future consolidation opportunities while deploying liquidity to modernize its fleet and support equity valuation.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mortgage rates are a little lower this morning, and where they'll go next isn't totally clear.
    • Sources indicate that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 7.05% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates are a little lower this morning, and where they'll go next isn't totally clear.

    Sources indicate that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 7.05% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is eight basis points lower than yesterday and 33 basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    In a recent development, inflation data out this morning looks, at first glance, like bad news for mortgage rates. But depending on how markets react, we could actually see lower mortgage rates. Keep reading after the charts for all the details.

    Below are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for perspective.

    Recent findings suggest that P.S. Markets will be closed tomorrow for Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, and mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to latest inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Like I mentioned above, it's not totally obvious where mortgage rates will head next. Let's walk through the two scenarios.

    Here's why rates could go up: This morning, we got October's Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, also known as PCE. It's the last measure of inflation to come out each month, but it's also the Federal Reserve's preferred metric, so PCE gets a lot of attention.

    The stats came in mostly as predicted, though it's not like the predictions were good — inflation's been overly strong for a while. But the core year-over-year figure, which came in a tenth of a percent over predictions, could prove troublesome. Core PCE removes categories that can be extra volatile, so it's considered a measure that highlights the underlying trend. In this case, the underlying trend is Not Good.

    It's already pretty much a lock that we'll see a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting, because yes, raising the federal funds rate is the Fed's main tool for taming inflation. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but a rate-hiking cycle from the central bankers definitely keeps upward pressure on borrowing costs.

    Recent findings suggest that on the other hand, here's why that same inflation data could help rates go down: Over the past several days, we've watched the stock market go on a wild ride, with the Anthropic IPO and the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Yesterday, things weren't looking good for tech stocks, and these inflation numbers could make it even worse.

    The amount that tech companies have borrowed to fund AI buildout is a significant concern for investors, since companies will have to cover those costs before investors see any profits. It's already a substantial task, and if everything costs more thanks to inflation, it's that much harder.

    Recent findings suggest that this AI-related anxiety is rough on the stock market, but it's been a boon for Treasury bonds. More demand for bonds pushes up bond prices, which brings down bond yields (basically, the return investors get on a bond). Mortgage rates for 30-year loans are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury note, so here's why you care about all of this: Lower Treasury yields means lower mortgage rates, too. If investors keep stressing about inflation eating into tech profits, we could see mortgage rates continue to move lower.

    That was a lot of info on inflation, but inflation's not the only major metric influencing rates.

    Industry observers note that let's back up for a second. The Federal Reserve tries to keep the economy steady by focusing on two key goals, often referred to as the Fed's dual mandate. One side is price stability — keeping inflation reasonable. The other is maximum employment, meaning those who want to work are able to find jobs.

    Sources indicate that next week we'll shift our focus to the employment side of the Federal Reserve's mandate, because the first week of the month is always all about employment data. On Tuesday, Dec. 1, we'll kick things off with the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS). JOLTS can tip us off to trends in the labor market; stuff like whether folks are leaving jobs voluntarily or if companies have openings that are going unfilled.

    Recent findings suggest that on Wednesday, payroll firm ADP will release its monthly employment stats. ADP is looking at its own payroll data to get an idea of how the job market is growing or contracting. The numbers don't include the public sector, but ADP often provides a preview of how the jobs report will go.

    It has been revealed that the Employment Situation Summary, better known as the jobs report, drops on Friday. This is the substantial one, since it tells us the nation's unemployment rate. The jobs report's other major stat is, similar to ADP, how many jobs the economy added or lost in the previous month. Unlike ADP though, the jobs report is inclusive of everybody in the public and private sectors.

    Recent findings suggest that lately the labor market's been looking super healthy, which is great news for the economy but less positive for mortgage rates. When hiring's strong, the Fed can feel safer raising the federal funds rate (that's the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers adjust). Higher rates tend to discourage businesses from borrowing and expanding, so if the job market's on shaky footing, the central bankers are going to be cautious about raising the benchmark rate.

    Industry observers note that what we're seeing now though, where inflation is clearly the problem and employment's just fine, is a recipe for higher rates. Again, the Fed doesn't control mortgage rates, but the central bank being in rate-hike mode puts upward pressure on mortgage rates.

    If we were to see employment falter in this latest round of numbers, it still probably wouldn't change the Fed's proposal. That would be one poor month for the labor market versus months upon months of inflation running rampant — so yeah, they'll keep an eye on jobs, but inflation's still the scourge.

    Our most likely source of lower mortgage rates in the short term is what I described above; investors who are leery of inflation and the promise of AI looking to the safe harbor of the bond market.

    » Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.55% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

    In a recent development, also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    Industry observers note that if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    Recent findings suggest that nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    Sources indicate that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    Ready for ‘The Great Lock In’? Viral Money Trend Can Improve Focus

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • When it’s cold outside, it’s the ideal time to stay home, organize your finances, set some latest money goals and make progress toward them.
    • That’s the promise of the viral winter money trend known as “The Great Lock In” that’s circulating on social media.
    • “You’re probably not doing too much,” notes Robert Baird, wealth manager at Cornerstone Financial Services in Southfield, Michigan.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When it’s cold outside, it’s the ideal time to stay home, organize your finances, set some latest money goals and make progress toward them.

    That’s the promise of the viral winter money trend known as “The Great Lock In” that’s circulating on social media.

    “You’re probably not doing too much,” notes Robert Baird, wealth manager at Cornerstone Financial Services in Southfield, Michigan. “It gets dark early. So those can be great months to lock into saving and not spend in excess.”.

    One vital component of the Great Lock In is developing upcoming routines that will last well into 2027, states Jordan Mangaliman, founder and fiduciary wealth advisor at GoldLine Wealth Management in Fullerton, California.

    Industry observers note that “We want a long-term habit versus a Band-Aid fix,” he says. “In today’s economy, money goes in and out so blindingly fast.”.

    Industry observers note that ready to join the movement? Here’s how to get started.

    What’s your money moonshot? Maybe it’s paying off all your credit card debt or purchasing a home. Or spending less than you earn. Defining it is the first step toward achieving it.

    Sources indicate that “Spend a lot of time identifying what that goal is,” Baird indicates. “Everyone’s in a different position, so comparing yourself to what you see online might not be applicable.”.

    Even while setting ambitious money goals, it’s worth grounding them in reality, Mangaliman indicates.

    If you want to save a larger portion of your income, he suggests trying the latest saving pattern for a couple of months to see how it feels rather than saying you’ll do it forever and then getting frustrated.

    “It’s a marathon, not a sprint,” Mangaliman adds.

    Once you’ve outlined those substantial goals for your Great Lock In, create a budget to help you achieve them, Baird says.

    In a recent development, he suggests combing through your previous credit or debit card spending to see where your money is going. Then you can decide what you want to change or shift. Using a tool like the 50/30/20 budget calculator can also help. This approach allots 50% of take-home pay toward needs, 30% toward wants and 20% toward savings and debt payments beyond the minimum.

    Sources indicate that baird suggests including saving as a line item in your budget so you don’t forget to do it. “Building that cost into your budget will put you in a better position later,” he says.

    Any Great Lock In should include growing your savings, because that makes achieving other goals easier, Baird says.

    According to recent reports, “Maybe there’s something you could cut in the short term to build up that savings,” he says. Good targets include subscription services, food delivery, entertainment and travel costs.

    Saving more is especially challenging in today’s environment, when everyday expenses like gas are higher than they were a year ago.

    In a recent development, baird says that makes winter a good time to try to reduce costs. There can be fewer temptations to go out and spend money when the days are shorter and the temperatures are colder.

    According to recent reports, mangaliman recommends setting aside three to six months’ worth of expenses, although even a smaller amount is helpful. “Ultimately it’s about what you can afford,” he claims. “It’s the foundation of your financial house.”.

    Along with building savings, paying down high-interest debt is another pillar of the Great Lock In.

    With credit card interest rates higher than they were a few years ago, carrying credit card debt has gotten more expensive. “I would consider applying some savings to paying down debt, especially right now when your debt is costing you more than you can earn in savings,” Baird notes. (You still want to reserve an emergency fund to cover unexpected expenses.).

    “High-interest debt is one of the biggest thieves of wealth,” Mangaliman notes. And one way to avoid turning to debt again in the future is to build up that emergency fund so it’s there for you if you need it.

    Even when you are committed to a Great Lock In, some hiccups along the way are inevitable. Success depends on continuing anyway.

    “It’s like a diet,” Baird says. “Just because you ate ice cream on a Sunday doesn’t mean on Monday you can’t go right back to being disciplined again.”.

    Sources indicate that “Be kind to yourself and do everything in moderation,” Mangaliman suggests. Just wanting to improve your finances is already a great first step, he indicates.

    In a recent development, in fact, he embraces the Great Lock In mentality himself. “There’s an old saying: It’s not how you start, but how you finish,” he indicates. “And you want to finish the year on a strong note so you carry those habits into 2027 and beyond.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    In a recent development, here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly vital sources of transaction revenue, while the tech giant has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    4 Ways to Prep Your Finances Before the Next Tech Outage

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If your social media feed is anything like mine, you’ve probably seen a reel or two on nonperishable food and solar-powered generators after the recent string of tech outages.
    • Recent findings suggest that have I considered giving water-filtering straws as stocking stuffers this year?
    • According to recent reports, but what about your money?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If your social media feed is anything like mine, you’ve probably seen a reel or two on nonperishable food and solar-powered generators after the recent string of tech outages.

    Recent findings suggest that have I considered giving water-filtering straws as stocking stuffers this year? Maybe.

    According to recent reports, but what about your money? If your area was hit by a natural disaster or your bank had an outage, are your finances ready?

    Industry observers note that dan Stanush, senior financial planner at Charles Schwab in Asheville, North Carolina, recalls how fast financial conveniences disappeared after Hurricane Helene hit in 2024. “We lost power for three weeks and water for six weeks,” he noted in an email. “And some local businesses could only accept cash or checks because card systems and ATMs were down.”.

    Don’t get caught unprepared. Here are the moves experts suggest to help you weather various types of emergencies:.

    According to recent reports, last week’s Chase outage was a good reminder that access to your bank balance can be disrupted. Stash at least enough cash at home — in small bills — to cover one week of expenses, says Jeff Judge, a certified financial planner (CFP) with Chesapeake Financial Planners in Forest Hill, Maryland.

    Sources indicate that if systems go down, ATMs can go down with them, said Eileen Olson, a CFP with Emerald Wealth in Daufuskie Island, South Carolina, in an email. Keeping cash in a safe at home is a good plan, but it’s also smart to carry cash when you travel. (Remember when planes were grounded nationwide a week and a half ago?).

    Recent findings suggest that “My parents and sister were traveling overseas on 9/11 and got stuck much longer than they expected,” Olson said. “After that, they always traveled with more cash.”.

    Sources indicate that if your primary bank and its app were down, would you be able to pay bills? Having an account at more than one bank gives you an alternate funding source. Consider opening a high-yield savings account at a second bank or credit union for your emergency fund.

    “This is the step I push hardest,” Judge notes. “I had a client whose debit card, credit card and savings all ran through one bank, so when that bank’s system went down, she couldn’t even buy gas.”.

    Recent findings suggest that if you don’t want to open a second bank account, a second credit card from a different bank and preferably on a different network (i.e. Visa vs. Mastercard) can provide another way to pay for things. “If there’s a problem with one credit card network, I have a backup with two other credit cards,” indicates Tony Steuer, author of “Get Ready! A Step-by-Step Planner for Maintaining Your Financial First Aid Kit.”.

    Make a printed list of your accounts, along with account numbers and key contact numbers. Include your bank, insurers, credit card companies and any financial professionals. Store the list with copies of essential paperwork, including insurance policies and their declarations pages, estate planning documents, legal certificates and identification — potentially in a fire-resistant file box.

    According to recent reports, keep a digital copy of your documents in a password-protected, encrypted spot as well. A password manager can store all of your login info.

    Joon Um, a CFP with Secure Tax & Accounting in Beverly Hills, California, suggests digital storage site Everplans to his clients, but there are a variety of sites that offer encrypted document storage.

    Sources indicate that take some time to write down how you’d pay for groceries, gas and medication if your usual payment methods weren’t available. What expenses would you need to cover first? What recurring bills are on autopay? Where would you keep the cash and any key documents you’d want to take with you if you had to leave home? Make sure other household members know where everything is.

    Industry observers note that and set a reminder to update your records at regular intervals. Steuer, for instance, saves his account statements as PDFs and prints everything out once a year. “One of the substantial concerns is that people could conceivably break into your 401(k) and drain your 401(k) account,” he notes. Account statements could help if a hack affects any financial balances.

    It all adds up to a web of protection that (hopefully) you’ll never have to use.

    “The goal is not to anticipate every scenario,” said Schwab's Dan Stanush, “but to have enough flexibility to meet basic needs while systems come back online.”.

    Industry News: Strategy Just Bought Bitcoin for the 4th Straight Week. So Why Aren't Crypto Investors Bullish on MSTR Stock?

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (657 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Strategy (MSTR +3.23%) has now bought Bitcoin (BTC -0.57%) four weeks in a row, with the most recent purchase disclosed on Nov.
    • Sources indicate that the share price tells a different story.
    • Sources indicate that although Strategy has consistently purchased Bitcoin in November, it's not buying much, especially compared to past acquisitions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Lyle Daly – Nov 27, 2026 at 8:43AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Strategy ›.

    Strategy (MSTR +3.23%) has now bought Bitcoin (BTC -0.57%) four weeks in a row, with the most recent purchase disclosed on Nov. 23. Considering that Strategy is the largest Bitcoin treasury company, you might think investors would be happy about this buying streak.

    Sources indicate that the share price tells a different story. Shares of Strategy reached a 52-week low of about $70 on Nov. 25, before rebounding to close at $80. Even after that recovery, Strategy stock is still down 39% since the start of the month. The Bitcoin acquisition approach has worked in the past, but this time, it feels more like a token gesture.

    Sources indicate that although Strategy has consistently purchased Bitcoin in November, it's not buying much, especially compared to past acquisitions. Over the past four weeks, it has bought 2,789 BTC, and the last two purchases were the smallest: 485 reported on Nov. 16 and 457 on Nov. 23.

    Those acquisitions account for just 0.3% of Strategy's total Bitcoin holdings, comprising 851,305 BTC. It's buying significantly less than it did earlier this year. For comparison, it bought 56,235 BTC in April and 25,404 BTC in May.

    Strategy operates a Bitcoin flywheel model, using equity, debt, and preferred securities to raise funds for Bitcoin purchases. Its stock previously traded at a premium to Bitcoin, which facilitated this approach. For much of 2024, Strategy's market valuation relative to the Bitcoin it held, or market-to-net-asset-value (mNAV) ratio, ranged from 2 times to 3 times. It could take advantage of that premium by issuing fresh shares and using the funds to buy Bitcoin.

    The company's mNAV has compressed to 0.94 times. Below 1, every share Strategy issues to buy Bitcoin dilutes shareholders.

    In addition, most of the funds Strategy has raised from recent share sales haven't gone toward Bitcoin. They've moved toward buying back Stretch (STRC +1.00%), a preferred stock aimed at investors seeking passive income. Stretch is designed to trade near a $100 par value and had slipped into the mid-$90s. Leaving it there would threaten Strategy's ability to issue more preferred shares to fund future Bitcoin buys, so the company is supporting the share price with buybacks.

    Recent findings suggest that from Nov. 16 to Nov. 22, Strategy sold 1,925,676 common shares, raising $176.7 million in net proceeds. It directed $147.0 million (83.2%) of those proceeds toward buying back Stretch shares -- alongside another $64.8 million from its cash reserves, for a total preferred buyback of $211.8 million -- while putting just $29.6 million (16.8%) toward Bitcoin. The priority has switched from acquiring as much Bitcoin as possible to defending the preferred stock.

    NASDAQ · As of 10:39 AM ET 11/27/26.

    Strategy is in a difficult position. MSCI unveiled that it will remove Strategy from its global indexes, including the MSCI USA index, at the close on Nov. 30. JPMorgan Chase projects that the exit will lead to $2.8 billion in forced selling. Strategy is also underwater on its Bitcoin holdings, with an average cost of $75,446 per Bitcoin, nearly 25% more than it trades at now.

    If you're bullish on Bitcoin, owning it directly or through Bitcoin ETFs is the safer option. Strategy served as a leveraged bet on Bitcoin in the past. Now, it needs to keep paying dividends on its preferred stock no matter how Bitcoin performs, and there's no telling if Strategy will be able to trade at a premium to Bitcoin again.
